{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YC89HHZzMjHvmPtVvfDJh2","type":"tool_result","content":"These `ptbk coder` options may be referenced in page prose and must be described accurately:\n\n-   `--harness <name>` — selects the coding agent; one of the harnesses in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md). Required when `run` or `server` executes prompts, and an optional filter for `list`.\n-   `--model <model>` — model passed to the harness; **required** for `openai-codex`, `gemini`, and `qwen-code` when they execute prompts, and an optional filter for `list`. The value `default` asks for the default model of that harness; for `openai-codex` it passes no model to Codex at all, so Codex keeps the model of its own configuration — the only thing a ChatGPT-account login accepts.\n-   Prompt routing — add one or more backtick-delimited model, model-family, harness, or selected-agent references to a ready `[ ]` status line, for example `` [ ] use model `gpt-5.5` `` or `` [ ] use agent `developer` ``. The prompt runs when any token matches after normalization, while `!` markers can appear before or after a token. A selected Book agent matches by its configured path (`agents/coding/developer.book`), filename (`developer.book`), filename without `.book` (`developer`), or title from the Book's first line (`Developer Foo bar`).\n-   `ptbk coder list` — list all ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority groups without starting a harness or changing files. Optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and `--max-priority` filters preview the queue a selected runner would receive.\n-   Prompt statuses — `[-]` or `[.]` not ready, `[ ]` ready, `[^]` being implemented right now, `[x]` implemented, verified and committed, `[!]` failed. A prompt with no status checkbox is also ready at priority `0`; when processing begins, its new `[^]` line is added before the prompt content. Put `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown file to ignore that entire file. `run` and `server` rewrite `[^]` before every step of a round, so it names the harness, the model, the finished steps and the running one (for example `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress ``). Only the final `[x]` is committed, and `[^]` is never reverted, so a killed or crashed coder leaves it behind as the signal that the task was left in the middle; such a prompt is not picked up again automatically.\n-   `--thinking-level <level>` — reasoning effort for supported harnesses: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`.\n-   `--agent <path.book>` — a `.book` file whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt and whose path, filename, filename without `.book`, and Book title can route agent-specific prompts. It also filters `ptbk coder list` without starting a harness.\n-   `--context <text-or-file>` — extra instructions inline or from a project file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`).\n-   `--test <command...>` — verification command run after each prompt; failures are fed back and retried.\n-   `--test-before <no|yes-and-fail|yes-and-fix>` — run the test command before coding; stop on pre-existing failures or create one repair prompt, and use `npm test` when no `--test` command is provided.\n-   `--dry-run` — print unwritten prompts without executing.\n-   `ptbk coder ping` — send one tiny dummy prompt to the harness and model selected with `--harness`, `--model` and `--thinking-level` and report the answer, the response time and the reported usage. It runs no coding task or commit; when the selected harness has missing local ignore rules, it asks before adding them to `.gitignore`. `--allow-credits` and `--no-ui` behave as for `run`, where `--no-ui` streams the raw harness output instead of the compact result.\n-   `--period <duration>` — `ping` only; instead of pinging once, keep pinging once per period until the process is stopped with `CTRL+C`. The duration uses the same format as the `--wait-*` options (`5h`, `30m`, `1h30m`) and must be positive. The period is measured from the start of one ping to the start of the next one, so `--period 5h` really pings every 5 hours regardless of how long a ping takes, and a failed ping is reported without ending the loop. Its main use is keeping the 5-hour quota window of Claude Code permanently open for the price of a few tokens per ping.\n-   `--min-priority <n>`, `--max-priority <n>` — for `run`, process only prompts within the inclusive priority range; for `list`, show only prompts within that range; `--priority <n>` remains an alias for `--min-priority`; for `add`, `--priority <n>` sets the priority of the new prompt (rendered as trailing `!` markers).\n-   `--limit <n>` — stop after N prompt runs (`run` only).\n-   `--count <n>` / `--count <n>*<m>` — `generate-boilerplates` only; number of generated prompt files, optionally with the number of prompts written into each of them. `--count N` is the same as `--count N*1`, the default is `5*1`, and more than one prompt per file is an advanced option: each of the `M` prompts is a separate task, separated by a `---` line, and shares the file's fresh emoji tag.\n-   `--no-auto` — wait for user confirmation before each prompt. Cannot be combined with `--no-questions`, which forbids the very confirmation it waits for.\n-   `--no-questions` — never ask an interactive question, taken by `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server`. Every optional step which needs an answer is skipped and reported together with the command which does it manually: installing a missing coding harness, updating an outdated harness, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing harness ignore rules to `.gitignore`. Because an outdated harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, the npm latest-version lookup is skipped as well, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it.\n-   `--no-commit`, `--git-changes <mode>`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git behavior switches of `run` and `server`, which commit every successful round by default.\n-   `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` — what happens when the working tree has uncommitted changes before a prompt starts. `fail` (the default) refuses to start and asks for a commit, a stash or one of the other two modes. `ignore` starts anyway and leaves the changes where they are. `continue` resumes the prompt an interrupted coder left behind in the `[^]` status, keeping its half-finished changes in place; it expects **exactly one** `[^]` prompt and fails when it finds none or more than one. Only that first round runs on the dirty tree, every later round expects a clean one again, and `continue` cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree would leave the uncommitted changes behind.\n-   Prompt status attribution — a prompt one harness started and another one continued records them in chronological order, as `` by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` ``, in its `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status line alike. Every later continuation appends another `interrupted, continued by …` report instead of dropping an earlier harness.\n-   `--order <from-earliest|from-latest|random>` — `verify` only; order in which the prompt files are walked through. `from-earliest` (the default) starts with the oldest prompt file, `from-latest` starts with the newest one, and `random` shuffles the queue for every pass.\n-   `--commit`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git synchronization of `init`, `add`, `generate-boilerplates` and `verify`, which never touch git unless these flags are used. `--auto-pull` pulls before the command changes anything, `--commit` commits the resulting changes with the coding-agent git identity, and `--auto-push` (which requires `--commit`) pushes the created commit. For `verify` the synchronization is applied around each single verification instead of once per run.\n-   Every commit `ptbk coder` creates contains **only the files of the operation which created it** — the added prompt file for `add`, the archived or repaired prompt file for `verify`, the prompt file together with the files the coding agent has changed for `run` and `server`. Changes which were already in the working tree before the command started are left there, so an unrelated work in progress is never swept into a coder commit.\n-   `--isolate` — `run` only; implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree (`.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>`) with its own copy of `.env`. A verified task is merged back into the current branch as one commit and the worktree is deleted; a task that cannot be merged is marked `[!]`, the failure is committed, and its worktree is kept for a manual merge while the coder continues. Because the worktree nests the whole repository one level deeper, git long path support is enabled for the isolated run so that Windows `MAX_PATH` does not break the checkout. Cannot be combined with `--no-commit`.\n-   `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-error <duration>` — wall-clock pacing; durations like `1h`, `30m`, `5s`; pause and computer sleep count against the wait; `S` skips whatever the coder waits for while `S Skip current waiting` is offered, which besides these three waits covers the harness session-limit wait and the `server` keep-alive poll; errors retry up to 3 times (default wait `10m`).\n-   `--no-ui`, `--preserve-logs` — plain streaming output / keep temp artifacts.\n-   `--port <port>` — `server` only; kanban UI port, default `4441`.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"924b3b1a-89cb-4373-9107-7e82d1ae2c4b","uuid":"efb05214-9dd5-4861-96df-c18cd5677db2","timestamp":"2026-09-14T17:41:33.340Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"These `ptbk coder` options may be referenced in page prose and must be described accurately:\n\n-   `--harness <name>` — selects the coding agent; one of the harnesses in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md). A prompt without a status marker is ready at priority `0`; when the coder starts it, the first live status line is added before its content and then rewritten as the task moves along:\n\n| Marker | Meaning                                       |\n| ------ | --------------------------------------------- |\n| `[-]`  | Not ready to be picked up at all              |\n| `[ ]`  | Ready, waiting for the next free coding round |\n| `[^]`  | Being implemented right now                   |\n| `[x]`  | Implemented, verified and committed           |\n| `[!]`  | Failed                                        |\n\nThe `[^]` in-progress status is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the steps which already finished and the step which is running:\n\n```text\n[ ]\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress\n[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nOnly the final `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: when the coder is killed or crashes, the prompt file keeps `[^]` as the signal that this task was left in the middle of its implementation. Such a prompt is not picked up again automatically — decide yourself whether to reset it to `[ ]`, to keep the partial work, or to resume it with `--git-changes continue`.\n\n## Run traces\n\nEvery round writes a run trace into `prompts/traces/`, named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to (`prompts/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md` is traced in `prompts/traces/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md`, and a prompt file holding more than one section appends the same `-2` suffix its temporary scripts use).\n\nEach trace pairs the metadata of the round with the untouched runtime log of the harness:\n\n-   the prompt it implemented, and which section of it when its file holds more than one,\n-   whether the round succeeded or failed,\n-   the harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,\n-   how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran,\n-   the verification command, when one is configured,\n-   when it started, when it finished and how long it took,\n-   the error which ended a failed round,","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"924b3b1a-89cb-4373-9107-7e82d1ae2c4b","uuid":"8ea64cbe-c397-4c16-a209-93465759b4f6","timestamp":"2026-09-14T17:41:38.258Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"## Prompt statuses\n\nEvery prompt can start with a checklist marker on its first line. availableModels?: ReadonlyArray<string>;\n    exampleUsages: ReadonlyArray<string>;\n}): string | TDefaultModel {\n    if (!options.providedModel) {\n        exitForMissingModel(options.agentName, options.providedModel;\n}\n\n/**\n * Prints the missing-model guidance and exits with the historical non-zero status code.\n */\nfunction exitForMissingModel(\n    agentName: ModelRequiringHarnessName,\n    availableModels: ReadonlyArray<string> | undefined,\n    exampleUsages: ReadonlyArray<string>,\n): never {\n    console.error(colors.red(`Error: --model is required model of availableModels) {\n            console.error(colors.gray(`  - ${model}`));\n        }\n        console.error('');\n    }\n\n    console.error(colors.cyan('Example usage:'));\n    for (const exampleUsage of exampleUsages) {\n        console.error(colors.gray(`  ${exampleUsage}`));\n    }\n\n    process.exit(1);\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":36,"oldLines":14,"newStart":36,"newLines":6,"lines":[" type ModelRequiringHarnessName = (typeof MODEL_REQUIRING_HARNESS_NAMES)[number];"," "," );\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads the chronological harness report left on the prompt before this round rewrites its in-progress status.\n *\n * Only a prompt resumed through `--git-changes continue` still uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n    waitForRequestedPause: WaitForCoderRunPauseCheckpoint;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const {\n        options: runOptions,\n        error,\n        attemptedRetries,\n        isRichUiEnabled,\n        progressDisplay,\n        uiHandle,\n        waitForRequestedPause,\n    } = options;\n\n    const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n\n    uiHandle?.state.addError(errorMessage);\n    uiHandle?.state.setPhase('waiting');\n\n    if (!isRichUiEnabled) {\n        console.warn(\n            colors.yellow(\n                `Prompt round failed (retry ${attemptedRetries}/${MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR}): ${errorMessage}`,\n            ),\n        );\n    }\n\n    const retryDeadlineTimeMs = Date.now() + runOptions.waitAfterError;\n\n    await waitForRequestedPause({\n        checkpointLabel: 'waiting after error before retrying the prompt',\n        phase: 'waiting',\n        statusMessage: `Waiting before retry ${attemptedRetries}/${MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS_AFTER_ERROR} after error`,\n    });\n\n    progressDisplay?.pauseTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.pauseTimer();\n\n    await sleepWithCountdown({\n progressDisplay?.resumeTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.resumeTimer();\n    uiHandle?.state.setPhase('running');\n    uiHandle?.state.setStatusMessage(`Retrying prompt (retry setPromptRoundRunningState(options: {\n    isRichUiEnabled: boolean;\n    promptLabel: string;\n    scriptPath: string;\n    uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n}): void {\n    const { isRichUiEnabled, uiHandle?: CoderRunUiHandle;\n    waitForRequestedPause: WaitForCoderRunPauseCheckpoint;\n    roundProjectPath: string;\n}): Promise<void> {\n    const {\n        options: runOptions,\n        nextPrompt,\n        runnerMetadata,\n        previousRunnerSignatures,\n        promptExecutionStartedDate,\n        result,\n        commitMessage,\n        logPath,\n        roundCommitScope,\n        isRichUiEnabled,\n        progressDisplay,\n        uiHandle,\n        waitForRequestedPause,\n        roundProjectPath,\n    } = options;\n\n    uiHandle?.stopCapturingAgentOutput();\n    await {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Q7meFWbbKrb5zATJTx5UER","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport moment from 'moment';\n2\timport { spaceTrim } from 'spacetrim';\n3\timport type { Usage } from '../../../src/execution/Usage';\n4\timport { ZERO_USAGE } from '../../../src/execution/utils/usage-constants';\n5\timport type { CoderRunStep } from '../common/CoderRunStep';\n6\timport { markPromptDone } from './markPromptDone';\n7\timport { markPromptFailed } from './markPromptFailed';\n8\timport { markPromptInProgress } from './markPromptInProgress';\n9\timport { parsePromptFile } from './parsePromptFile';\n10\t\n11\t/**\n12\t * Number of milliseconds in one minute, used to build readable step durations in these tests.\n13\t */\n14\tconst ONE_MINUTE_MS = 60 * 1000;\n15\t\n16\t/**\n17\t * Builds a usage record with a concrete, certain price for the in-progress status tests.\n18\t */\n19\tfunction createUsageWithPrice(price: number): Usage {\n20\t    return { ...ZERO_USAGE, price: { value: price } };\n21\t}\n22\t\n23\t/**\n24\t * Builds the finished implementation step shared by the multi-step tests.\n25\t */\n26\tfunction createImplementationStep(): CoderRunStep {\n27\t    return { kind: 'implementation', usage: createUsageWithPrice(0.2036), durationMs: 10 * ONE_MINUTE_MS };\n28\t}\n29\t\n30\t/**\n31\t * Parses one single-prompt file used by these tests.\n32\t */\n33\tfunction createPromptFile(statusLine: string) {\n34\t    const file = parsePromptFile(\n35\t        'prompts/mark-prompt-in-progress.md',\n36\t        spaceTrim(`\n37\t            ${statusLine}\n38\t            Implement the feature\n39\t        `),\n40\t    );\n41\t\n42\t    return { file, section: file.sections[0]! };\n43\t}\n44\t\n45\tdescribe('markPromptInProgress', () => {\n46\t    it('turns a todo prompt into an in-progress prompt naming the started step', () => {\n47\t        const { file, section } = createPromptFile('[ ]');\n48\t\n49\t        markPromptInProgress({\n50\t            file,\n51\t            section,\n52\t            steps: [],\n53\t            inProgressStepKind: 'implementation',\n54\t            runnerName: 'OpenAI Codex',\n55\t            modelName: 'gpt-5.6-luna',\n56\t            attemptCount: 1,\n57\t            thinkingLevel: 'max',\n58\t        });\n59\t\n60\t        expect(file.lines[0]).toBe('[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress');\n61\t    });\n62\t\n63\t    it('adds the live status line before an unmarked prompt and later replaces it when the prompt is done', () => {\n64\t        const file = parsePromptFile(\n65\t            'prompts/unmarked-prompt.md',\n66\t            spaceTrim(`\n67\t                Implement the feature\n68\t\n69\t                Preserve this prompt content.\n70\t            `),\n71\t        );\n72\t        const section = file.sections[0]!;\n73\t\n74\t        markPromptInProgress({\n75\t            file,\n76\t            section,\n77\t            steps: [],\n78\t            inProgressStepKind: 'implementation',\n79\t            runnerName: 'OpenAI Codex',\n80\t            modelName: 'gpt-5.6-luna',\n81\t            attemptCount: 1,\n82\t        });\n83\t\n84\t        expect(file.lines).toEqual([\n85\t            '[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` - Implementation in progress',\n86\t            'Implement the feature',\n87\t            '',\n88\t            'Preserve this prompt content.',\n89\t        ]);\n90\t        expect(section.statusLineIndex).toBe(0);\n91\t\n92\t        markPromptDone({\n93\t            file,\n94\t            section,\n95\t            steps: [createImplementationStep()],\n96\t            runnerName: 'OpenAI Codex',\n97\t            modelName: 'gpt-5.6-luna',\n98\t            attemptCount: 1,\n99\t        });\n100\t\n101\t        expect(file.lines).toEqual([\n102\t            '[x] by {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EH2uMQ4Kkcy6FJCwiHdnGj","type":"tool_result","content":"136\t\n137\tThe `[^]` in-progress status is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the steps which already finished and the step which is running:\n138\t\n139\t```text\n140\t[ ]\n141\t[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n142\t[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress\n143\t[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n144\t```\n145\t\n146\tOnly the final `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: when the coder is killed or crashes, the prompt file keeps `[^]` as the signal that this task was left in the middle of its implementation. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"924b3b1a-89cb-4373-9107-7e82d1ae2c4b","uuid":"4f45fba6-7b1f-4681-af60-f111db354af0","timestamp":"2026-09-14T17:50:16.621Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/Users/hejny/work/promptbook/scripts/run-codex-prompts/README.md","oldString":"[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nOnly the final `[x]` state is committed,","newString":"[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nA run personalized with `--agent` names that agent in front of the harness which runs it, because the same harness and model behave differently depending on the agent they run as:\n\n```text\n[x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nOnly the final `[x]` state is committed,","originalFile":"# run-codex-prompts\n\n`run-codex-prompts.ts` drives the Coding Agent workflow. It loads the `prompts/` tasks, runs them through the selected model runner (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, etc.), and automatically writes, stages, commits, and optionally pushes the generated files.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Via Promptbook CLI (recommended):\n\n```bash\n# External usage (when promptbook is installed globally)\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n\n# Internal usage (within Promptbook repository)\nnpx ts-node ./src/cli/test/ptbk.ts coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n```\n\n### Direct execution (legacy):\n\n```bash\nnpx ts-node ./scripts/run-codex-prompts/run-codex-prompts.ts --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n```\n\n### Available options:\n\n```bash\n--dry-run                     # Print unwritten prompts without executing\n--harness <harness-name>        # Select runner: openai-codex, github-copilot, cline, claude-code, opencode, gemini (required for non-dry-run)\n--model <model>               # Model to use (required for openai-codex and gemini, optional for github-copilot and opencode)\n--context <context-or-file>   # Append extra instructions inline or load them from a file in the current project\n--test <test-command...>       # Run a verification command after each prompt and feed failures back for retries\n--test-before <mode>           # no (default), yes-and-fail, or yes-and-fix; enabled modes default to npm test\n--no-ui                       # Disable the rich terminal UI and stream plain console output instead\n--thinking-level <level>      # Reasoning effort for OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot: low, medium, high, xhigh\n--priority <minimum-priority> # Alias for --min-priority\n--min-priority <minimum-priority> # Filter prompts by minimum priority level\n--max-priority <maximum-priority> # Filter prompts by maximum priority level\n--allow-credits               # Allow OpenAI Codex runner to spend credits when limits are exhausted\n--isolate                     # Implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree and merge it back when verified\n--auto-push                  # Push each successful commit to the configured remote\n--auto-migrate                # Run testing-server DB migrations after each successful prompt\n--allow-destructive-auto-migrate # Override destructive SQL heuristic guard in auto-migrate mode\n--no-auto                     # Wait for user confirmation before each prompt instead of running automatically\n--wait-after-prompt <duration>    # Wait this long after each prompt finishes before starting the next prompt (default 0)\n--wait-between-prompts <duration> # Pace prompts so each next prompt starts at least this long after the previous start (default 0)\n--wait-after-error <duration>     # Wait this long before retrying after an error (up to 3 retries, default 10m)\n--git-changes <mode>          # Dirty working tree: fail (default), ignore the changes, or continue the interrupted [^] prompt\n--no-normalize-line-endings   # Disable per-round CRLF -> LF normalization for changed files\n```\n\nFor `--harness openai-codex`, credits are opt-in. If Codex reports that credits are required and `--allow-credits` is not set, the runner fails fast with a rerun hint.\n\n### Terminal controls\n\nThe `S` control is shown only while the coder is waiting; it is hidden while a prompt is running or after the run has finished.\n\n```text\nP  Pause  S  Skip current waiting  X  End with this prompt  CTRL+C  Exit\n```\n\nPress `X` again after requesting the dynamic end to continue the full current run.\n\nEvery press is answered right under the pills, so you never have to guess whether the key arrived:\n\n```text\n» S  Skipping the current waiting, continuing right now\n» S  Nothing to skip, the coder is not waiting right now (×2)\n```\n\nThe answer stays on screen for a few seconds and repeated identical answers are counted, so pressing the same control twice redraws the frame too. In `--no-ui` mode the very same line is printed to the console instead.\n\nWhenever `S  Skip current waiting` is offered, the wait really ends on that key press: the `--wait-between-prompts` and `--wait-after-prompt` pacing, the `--wait-after-error` cool-down, the Claude Code session-limit wait before a `--resume` resurrection, and the `ptbk coder server` keep-alive poll.\n\n### Examples:\n\n```bash\n# Dry run to preview prompts\nptbk coder run --dry-run\n\n# Run with OpenAI Codex\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n\n# Run with project instructions loaded from AGENTS.md\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md\n\n# Run with one-off inline instructions\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --context \"Focus only on src/cli\"\n\n# Run with OpenAI Codex and explicitly allow credit spending\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --allow-credits\n\n# Run with explicit post-commit git pushing\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --auto-push\n\n# Run with GitHub Copilot\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh\n\n# Run tests before coding and let one repair prompt fix pre-existing failures\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --test-before yes-and-fix\n\n# Run with plain streaming output for logging/debugging\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --no-ui\n\n# Run with Gemini\nptbk coder run --harness gemini --model gemini-3-flash-preview\n\n# Run with Claude Code\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code\n\n# Run with priority range filter\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --min-priority 1 --max-priority 5\n\n# Run with automatic testing-server migrations after each prompt\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --auto-migrate\n\n# Run each prompt in its own isolated git worktree\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --isolate\n\n# Start the next prompt even though the working tree still has uncommitted changes\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes ignore\n\n# Continue the one prompt a killed or crashed coder left behind in the [^] status\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes continue\n```\n\n## Prompt statuses\n\nEvery prompt can start with a checklist marker on its first line. A prompt without a status marker is ready at priority `0`; when the coder starts it, the first live status line is added before its content and then rewritten as the task moves along:\n\n| Marker | Meaning                                       |\n| ------ | --------------------------------------------- |\n| `[-]`  | Not ready to be picked up at all              |\n| `[ ]`  | Ready, waiting for the next free coding round |\n| `[^]`  | Being implemented right now                   |\n| `[x]`  | Implemented, verified and committed           |\n| `[!]`  | Failed                                        |\n\nThe `[^]` in-progress status is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the steps which already finished and the step which is running:\n\n```text\n[ ]\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress\n[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nOnly the final `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: when the coder is killed or crashes, the prompt file keeps `[^]` as the signal that this task was left in the middle of its implementation. Such a prompt is not picked up again automatically — decide yourself whether to reset it to `[ ]`, to keep the partial work, or to resume it with `--git-changes continue`.\n\n## Run traces\n\nEvery round writes a run trace into `prompts/traces/`, named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to (`prompts/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md` is traced in `prompts/traces/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md`, and a prompt file holding more than one section appends the same `-2` suffix its temporary scripts use).\n\nEach trace pairs the metadata of the round with the untouched runtime log of the harness:\n\n-   the prompt it implemented, and which section of it when its file holds more than one,\n-   whether the round succeeded or failed,\n-   the harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,\n-   how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran,\n-   the verification command, when one is configured,\n-   when it started, when it finished and how long it took,\n-   the error which ended a failed round,\n-   everything the harness and the verification command have written, including the generated shell scripts and the prompt they embed.\n\nThe trace is written before the round is committed, so it lands in the very same commit as the prompt it describes. This is the only place where the live runtime log survives — that log is a temporary artifact which is deleted as soon as a successful round is over (unless `--preserve-logs` keeps it). Re-running the same prompt overwrites its trace; the earlier ones stay in the git history.\n\n## Dirty working tree\n\n`--git-changes` decides what happens when the working tree still has uncommitted changes before a prompt starts:\n\n| Mode       | Behavior                                                                                                     |\n| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `fail`     | Refuses to start and asks for a commit, a stash or one of the other two modes (the default)                  |\n| `ignore`   | Starts the next `[ ]` prompt anyway and leaves the uncommitted changes where they are                        |\n| `continue` | Resumes the interrupted `[^]` prompt with its half-finished changes still in place                           |\n\n`continue` expects **exactly one** prompt in the `[^]` status and fails when it finds none or more than one, because the uncommitted changes could not be attributed to a single interrupted task. Only the resuming round runs on the dirty tree; once it is finished and committed, every later round expects a clean working tree again. It cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree is checked out from the last commit and would leave the uncommitted changes behind.\n\nThe harness which resumes the work does not have to be the one which started it. Its status report is built in\nchronological order and remains extendable if another run is interrupted later:\n\n```text\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high` - Implementation in progress\n[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high`\n```\n\nThe status still names the phase currently running, but it does not append a completed continuation's own cost and\nduration as though they measured the whole interrupted prompt.\n\n## Isolated runs\n\nWith `--isolate`, no prompt is ever implemented in the working tree you started the coder from:\n\n-   Each task gets a temporary git worktree in `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>` (for example `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/2026-07-0700-ptbk-coder-timing`).\n-   The worktree gets its own copy of the project `.env`, so the isolated task runs with its own environment.\n-   The coding agent, the `--test` verification command and the round commit all happen inside the worktree.\n-   Once the task is implemented and verified, it is merged back into the branch the coder runs on as one commit and the worktree plus its branch are deleted.\n-   If the merge fails, the task is marked as `[!]` instead of `[x]`, the failure is committed into the original worktree, the temporary worktree is kept for a manual merge, and the coder continues with the next task.\n\nBecause the worktrees live inside `.promptbook`, `--isolate` requires that folder to be git-ignored (`ptbk coder init` sets this up).\n\n## Agent identity configuration\n\nAll commits created by this script are signed with a dedicated agent identity. The helper in `scripts/run-codex-prompts/git/agentGitIdentity.ts` reads the following environment variables, so you can customize the identity per machine:\n\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GIT_NAME` – the `user.name` value that will appear on each commit.\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GIT_EMAIL` – the `user.email` value that will appear on each commit.\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GPG_KEY_ID` – the GPG key ID used to sign the commit (the key must exist in your local GPG keyring).\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GPG_PROGRAM` (optional) – override the GPG program if you do not want to use the default `gpg` binary.\n\nSet the values via `.env`, shell variables, or whichever secrets manager you prefer. The script will fail fast if the identity is missing so that commits cannot fall back to the primary user's configuration.\n\nIf you need a fresh agent key, generate it with GPG (for example from a temporary config file: specify `Name-Real`, `Name-Email`, `Key-Type`, `Key-Length`, `%no-protection`, and `%commit`) and set `CODING_AGENT_GPG_KEY_ID` to the new key's long ID.\n\nYou can bootstrap your environment with the \"Promptbook Coding Agent\" details (name `Promptbook Coding Agent`, email `coding-agent@promptbook.studio`, key ID `13406525ED912F938FEA85AB4046C687298B2382`), then swap them out whenever a different persona makes more sense.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":143,"oldLines":6,"newStart":143,"newLines":12,"lines":[" [x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes"," ```"," ","+A run personalized with `--agent` names that agent in front of the harness which runs it, because the same harness and model behave differently depending on the agent they run as:","+","+```text","+[x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes","+```","+"," Only the final `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: when the coder is killed or crashes, the prompt file keeps `[^]` as the signal that this task was left in the middle of its implementation. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CMaZQevwXSQhKQMfBHUq4K","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /Users/hejny/work/promptbook/scripts/run-codex-prompts/README.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"924b3b1a-89cb-4373-9107-7e82d1ae2c4b","uuid":"1303d3a3-7602-4712-b036-9658e8e4cda4","timestamp":"2026-09-14T17:50:21.944Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/Users/hejny/work/promptbook/scripts/run-codex-prompts/README.md","oldString":"-   the harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,","newString":"-   the Book agent, harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,","originalFile":"# run-codex-prompts\n\n`run-codex-prompts.ts` drives the Coding Agent workflow. It loads the `prompts/` tasks, runs them through the selected model runner (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, etc.), and automatically writes, stages, commits, and optionally pushes the generated files.\n\n## Usage\n\n### Via Promptbook CLI (recommended):\n\n```bash\n# External usage (when promptbook is installed globally)\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n\n# Internal usage (within Promptbook repository)\nnpx ts-node ./src/cli/test/ptbk.ts coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n```\n\n### Direct execution (legacy):\n\n```bash\nnpx ts-node ./scripts/run-codex-prompts/run-codex-prompts.ts --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n```\n\n### Available options:\n\n```bash\n--dry-run                     # Print unwritten prompts without executing\n--harness <harness-name>        # Select runner: openai-codex, github-copilot, cline, claude-code, opencode, gemini (required for non-dry-run)\n--model <model>               # Model to use (required for openai-codex and gemini, optional for github-copilot and opencode)\n--context <context-or-file>   # Append extra instructions inline or load them from a file in the current project\n--test <test-command...>       # Run a verification command after each prompt and feed failures back for retries\n--test-before <mode>           # no (default), yes-and-fail, or yes-and-fix; enabled modes default to npm test\n--no-ui                       # Disable the rich terminal UI and stream plain console output instead\n--thinking-level <level>      # Reasoning effort for OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot: low, medium, high, xhigh\n--priority <minimum-priority> # Alias for --min-priority\n--min-priority <minimum-priority> # Filter prompts by minimum priority level\n--max-priority <maximum-priority> # Filter prompts by maximum priority level\n--allow-credits               # Allow OpenAI Codex runner to spend credits when limits are exhausted\n--isolate                     # Implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree and merge it back when verified\n--auto-push                  # Push each successful commit to the configured remote\n--auto-migrate                # Run testing-server DB migrations after each successful prompt\n--allow-destructive-auto-migrate # Override destructive SQL heuristic guard in auto-migrate mode\n--no-auto                     # Wait for user confirmation before each prompt instead of running automatically\n--wait-after-prompt <duration>    # Wait this long after each prompt finishes before starting the next prompt (default 0)\n--wait-between-prompts <duration> # Pace prompts so each next prompt starts at least this long after the previous start (default 0)\n--wait-after-error <duration>     # Wait this long before retrying after an error (up to 3 retries, default 10m)\n--git-changes <mode>          # Dirty working tree: fail (default), ignore the changes, or continue the interrupted [^] prompt\n--no-normalize-line-endings   # Disable per-round CRLF -> LF normalization for changed files\n```\n\nFor `--harness openai-codex`, credits are opt-in. If Codex reports that credits are required and `--allow-credits` is not set, the runner fails fast with a rerun hint.\n\n### Terminal controls\n\nThe `S` control is shown only while the coder is waiting; it is hidden while a prompt is running or after the run has finished.\n\n```text\nP  Pause  S  Skip current waiting  X  End with this prompt  CTRL+C  Exit\n```\n\nPress `X` again after requesting the dynamic end to continue the full current run.\n\nEvery press is answered right under the pills, so you never have to guess whether the key arrived:\n\n```text\n» S  Skipping the current waiting, continuing right now\n» S  Nothing to skip, the coder is not waiting right now (×2)\n```\n\nThe answer stays on screen for a few seconds and repeated identical answers are counted, so pressing the same control twice redraws the frame too. In `--no-ui` mode the very same line is printed to the console instead.\n\nWhenever `S  Skip current waiting` is offered, the wait really ends on that key press: the `--wait-between-prompts` and `--wait-after-prompt` pacing, the `--wait-after-error` cool-down, the Claude Code session-limit wait before a `--resume` resurrection, and the `ptbk coder server` keep-alive poll.\n\n### Examples:\n\n```bash\n# Dry run to preview prompts\nptbk coder run --dry-run\n\n# Run with OpenAI Codex\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex\n\n# Run with project instructions loaded from AGENTS.md\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md\n\n# Run with one-off inline instructions\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --context \"Focus only on src/cli\"\n\n# Run with OpenAI Codex and explicitly allow credit spending\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --allow-credits\n\n# Run with explicit post-commit git pushing\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --auto-push\n\n# Run with GitHub Copilot\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh\n\n# Run tests before coding and let one repair prompt fix pre-existing failures\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --test-before yes-and-fix\n\n# Run with plain streaming output for logging/debugging\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --no-ui\n\n# Run with Gemini\nptbk coder run --harness gemini --model gemini-3-flash-preview\n\n# Run with Claude Code\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code\n\n# Run with priority range filter\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --min-priority 1 --max-priority 5\n\n# Run with automatic testing-server migrations after each prompt\nptbk coder run --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.2-codex --auto-migrate\n\n# Run each prompt in its own isolated git worktree\nptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --agent agents/coding/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --isolate\n\n# Start the next prompt even though the working tree still has uncommitted changes\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes ignore\n\n# Continue the one prompt a killed or crashed coder left behind in the [^] status\nptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes continue\n```\n\n## Prompt statuses\n\nEvery prompt can start with a checklist marker on its first line. A prompt without a status marker is ready at priority `0`; when the coder starts it, the first live status line is added before its content and then rewritten as the task moves along:\n\n| Marker | Meaning                                       |\n| ------ | --------------------------------------------- |\n| `[-]`  | Not ready to be picked up at all              |\n| `[ ]`  | Ready, waiting for the next free coding round |\n| `[^]`  | Being implemented right now                   |\n| `[x]`  | Implemented, verified and committed           |\n| `[!]`  | Failed                                        |\n\nThe `[^]` in-progress status is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the steps which already finished and the step which is running:\n\n```text\n[ ]\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress\n[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nA run personalized with `--agent` names that agent in front of the harness which runs it, because the same harness and model behave differently depending on the agent they run as:\n\n```text\n[x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes\n```\n\nOnly the final `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: when the coder is killed or crashes, the prompt file keeps `[^]` as the signal that this task was left in the middle of its implementation. Such a prompt is not picked up again automatically — decide yourself whether to reset it to `[ ]`, to keep the partial work, or to resume it with `--git-changes continue`.\n\n## Run traces\n\nEvery round writes a run trace into `prompts/traces/`, named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to (`prompts/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md` is traced in `prompts/traces/2026-09-0180-ptbk-coder-save-traces.md`, and a prompt file holding more than one section appends the same `-2` suffix its temporary scripts use).\n\nEach trace pairs the metadata of the round with the untouched runtime log of the harness:\n\n-   the prompt it implemented, and which section of it when its file holds more than one,\n-   whether the round succeeded or failed,\n-   the harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,\n-   how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran,\n-   the verification command, when one is configured,\n-   when it started, when it finished and how long it took,\n-   the error which ended a failed round,\n-   everything the harness and the verification command have written, including the generated shell scripts and the prompt they embed.\n\nThe trace is written before the round is committed, so it lands in the very same commit as the prompt it describes. This is the only place where the live runtime log survives — that log is a temporary artifact which is deleted as soon as a successful round is over (unless `--preserve-logs` keeps it). Re-running the same prompt overwrites its trace; the earlier ones stay in the git history.\n\n## Dirty working tree\n\n`--git-changes` decides what happens when the working tree still has uncommitted changes before a prompt starts:\n\n| Mode       | Behavior                                                                                                     |\n| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `fail`     | Refuses to start and asks for a commit, a stash or one of the other two modes (the default)                  |\n| `ignore`   | Starts the next `[ ]` prompt anyway and leaves the uncommitted changes where they are                        |\n| `continue` | Resumes the interrupted `[^]` prompt with its half-finished changes still in place                           |\n\n`continue` expects **exactly one** prompt in the `[^]` status and fails when it finds none or more than one, because the uncommitted changes could not be attributed to a single interrupted task. Only the resuming round runs on the dirty tree; once it is finished and committed, every later round expects a clean working tree again. It cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree is checked out from the last commit and would leave the uncommitted changes behind.\n\nThe harness which resumes the work does not have to be the one which started it. Its status report is built in\nchronological order and remains extendable if another run is interrupted later:\n\n```text\n[^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high` - Implementation in progress\n[x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high`\n```\n\nThe status still names the phase currently running, but it does not append a completed continuation's own cost and\nduration as though they measured the whole interrupted prompt.\n\n## Isolated runs\n\nWith `--isolate`, no prompt is ever implemented in the working tree you started the coder from:\n\n-   Each task gets a temporary git worktree in `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>` (for example `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/2026-07-0700-ptbk-coder-timing`).\n-   The worktree gets its own copy of the project `.env`, so the isolated task runs with its own environment.\n-   The coding agent, the `--test` verification command and the round commit all happen inside the worktree.\n-   Once the task is implemented and verified, it is merged back into the branch the coder runs on as one commit and the worktree plus its branch are deleted.\n-   If the merge fails, the task is marked as `[!]` instead of `[x]`, the failure is committed into the original worktree, the temporary worktree is kept for a manual merge, and the coder continues with the next task.\n\nBecause the worktrees live inside `.promptbook`, `--isolate` requires that folder to be git-ignored (`ptbk coder init` sets this up).\n\n## Agent identity configuration\n\nAll commits created by this script are signed with a dedicated agent identity. The helper in `scripts/run-codex-prompts/git/agentGitIdentity.ts` reads the following environment variables, so you can customize the identity per machine:\n\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GIT_NAME` – the `user.name` value that will appear on each commit.\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GIT_EMAIL` – the `user.email` value that will appear on each commit.\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GPG_KEY_ID` – the GPG key ID used to sign the commit (the key must exist in your local GPG keyring).\n-   `CODING_AGENT_GPG_PROGRAM` (optional) – override the GPG program if you do not want to use the default `gpg` binary.\n\nSet the values via `.env`, shell variables, or whichever secrets manager you prefer. The script will fail fast if the identity is missing so that commits cannot fall back to the primary user's configuration.\n\nIf you need a fresh agent key, generate it with GPG (for example from a temporary config file: specify `Name-Real`, `Name-Email`, `Key-Type`, `Key-Length`, `%no-protection`, and `%commit`) and set `CODING_AGENT_GPG_KEY_ID` to the new key's long ID.\n\nYou can bootstrap your environment with the \"Promptbook Coding Agent\" details (name `Promptbook Coding Agent`, email `coding-agent@promptbook.studio`, key ID `13406525ED912F938FEA85AB4046C687298B2382`), then swap them out whenever a different persona makes more sense.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":159,"oldLines":7,"newStart":159,"newLines":7,"lines":[" "," -   the prompt it implemented, and which section of it when its file holds more than one,"," -   whether the round succeeded or failed,","--   the harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,","+-   the Book agent, harness, model, thinking level and login method which ran it,"," -   how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran,"," -   the verification command, when one is configured,"," -   when it started, when it finished and how long it took,"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

a dark mode toggle to the settings page\"`                                                                                                                                         | [Quickstart step           | `ptbk coder list`                                                                                                                                                                                      | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md), [Quickstart step 4](../sections/quickstart.md) |\n| `GENERATE_BOILERPLATES_COMMAND` | `ptbk coder generate-boilerplates --count 10*7`                                                                                                                                                        | [Advanced `AGENT_FILTER_COMMAND`          | `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.5 --agent agents/developer.book`                                                                                                              | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `TEST_BEFORE_FIX_COMMAND`       | `ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --test npm test --test-before yes-and-fix`                                                                                                                       | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `GIT_CHANGES_CONTINUE_COMMAND`  | `ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes continue` --dry-run`                                                                                                                                                                             | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `PING_COMMAND`                  | `ptbk coder ping --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.6-sol --thinking-level xhigh`                                                                                                                    | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `PING_PERIOD_COMMAND`           | `ptbk coder ping --harness claude-code --model claude-sonnet-5 --thinking-level low --period 5h`                                                                                                       | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `SERVER_COMMAND`                | `ptbk coder server --harness claude-code --model fable --thinking-level max --agent agents/developer.book --context AGENTS.md --test npm run test`                                                     | [Quickstart step 5](../sections/quickstart.md) \"npm run test-for-ptbk-coder\" --wait-between-prompts 4h --limit 1` | Typed in the [live terminal](../components/live-terminal.md)                |\n| `AGENT_RUN_COMMAND`             | `ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --model fable --agent agents/developer.book --context AGENTS.md`                                                                                                 | [Agent personas](../sections/agent-book.md)                                 |\n| `VERIFY_COMMAND`                | `ptbk coder verify --order from-latest`                                                                                                                                                                | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n\nPer-harness sample commands are defined in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md); per-feature snippets in [`../sections/advanced-features.md`](../sections/advanced-features.md).\n\n## Option reference (context for copywriting)\n\nThese `ptbk coder` options may be referenced in page prose and must be described accurately:\n\n-   `--harness <name>` — selects the coding agent; one of the harnesses in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md). Required when `run` or `server` executes prompts, and an optional filter for `list`.\n-   `--model <model>` — model passed to the harness; **required** for `openai-codex`, `gemini`, and `qwen-code` when they execute prompts, and an optional filter for `list`. The value `default` asks for the default model of that harness; for `openai-codex` it passes no model to Codex at all, so Codex keeps the model of its own configuration — the only thing a ChatGPT-account login accepts.\n-   Prompt routing — add one or more backtick-delimited model, model-family, harness, or selected-agent references to a ready `[ ]` status line, for example `` [ ] use model `gpt-5.5` `` or `` [ ] use agent `developer` ``. The prompt runs when any token matches after normalization, while `!` markers can appear before or after a token. A selected Book agent matches by its configured path (`agents/coding/developer.book`), filename (`developer.book`), filename without `.book` (`developer`), or title from the Book's first line (`Developer Foo bar`).\n-   `ptbk coder list` — list all ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority groups without starting a harness or changing files. Optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and `--max-priority` filters preview the queue a selected runner would receive.\n-   Prompt statuses — `[-]` or `[.]` not ready, `[ ]` ready, `[^]` being implemented right now, `[x]` implemented, verified and committed, `[!]` failed. A prompt with no status checkbox is also ready at priority `0`; when processing begins, its new `[^]` line is added before the prompt content. Put `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown file to ignore that entire file. `run` and `server` rewrite `[^]` before every step of a round, so it names the harness, the model, the finished steps and the running one (for example `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress ``). Only the final `[x]` is committed, and `[^]` is never reverted, so a killed or crashed coder leaves it behind as the signal that the task was left in the middle; such a prompt is not picked up again automatically.\n-   `--thinking-level <level>` — reasoning effort for supported harnesses: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`.\n-   `--agent <path.book>` — a `.book` file whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt and whose path, filename, filename without `.book`, and Book title can route agent-specific prompts. It also filters `ptbk coder list` without starting a harness.\n-   `--context <text-or-file>` — extra instructions inline or from a project file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`).\n-   `--test <command...>` — verification command run after each prompt; failures are fed back and retried.\n-   `--test-before <no|yes-and-fail|yes-and-fix>` — run the test command before coding; stop on pre-existing failures or create one repair prompt, and use `npm test` when no `--test` command is provided.\n-   `--dry-run` — print unwritten prompts without executing.\n-   `ptbk coder ping` — send one tiny dummy prompt to the harness and model selected with `--harness`, `--model` and `--thinking-level` and report the answer, the response time and the reported usage. It runs no coding task or commit; when the selected harness has missing local ignore rules, it asks before adding them to `.gitignore`. `--allow-credits` and `--no-ui` behave as for `run`, where `--no-ui` streams the raw harness output instead of the compact result.\n-   `--period <duration>` — `ping` only; instead of pinging once, keep pinging once per period until the process is stopped with `CTRL+C`. The duration uses the same format as the `--wait-*` options (`5h`, `30m`, `1h30m`) and must be positive. The period is measured from the start of one ping to the start of the next one, so `--period 5h` really pings every 5 hours regardless of how long a ping takes, and a failed ping is reported without ending the loop. Its main use is keeping the 5-hour quota window of Claude Code permanently open for the price of a few tokens per ping.\n-   `--min-priority <n>`, `--max-priority <n>` — for `run`, process only prompts within the inclusive priority range; for `list`, show only prompts within that range; `--priority <n>` remains an alias for `--min-priority`; for `add`, `--priority <n>` sets the priority of the new prompt (rendered as trailing `!` markers).\n-   `--limit <n>` — stop after N prompt runs (`run` only).\n-   `--count <n>` / `--count <n>*<m>` — `generate-boilerplates` only; number of generated prompt files, optionally with the number of prompts written into each of them. `--count N` is the same as `--count N*1`, the default is `5*1`, and more than one prompt per file is an advanced option: each of the `M` prompts is a separate task, separated by a `---` line, and shares the file's fresh emoji tag.\n-   `--no-auto` — wait for user confirmation before each prompt. Cannot be combined with `--no-questions`, which forbids the very confirmation it waits for.\n-   `--no-questions` — never ask an interactive question, taken by `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server`. Every optional step which needs an answer is skipped and reported together with the command which does it manually: installing a missing coding harness, updating an outdated harness, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing harness ignore rules to `.gitignore`. Because an outdated harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, the npm latest-version lookup is skipped as well, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it.\n-   `--no-commit`, `--git-changes <mode>`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git behavior switches of `run` and `server`, which commit every successful round by default.\n-   `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` — what happens when the working tree has uncommitted changes before a prompt starts. `fail` (the default) refuses to start and asks for a commit, a stash or one of the other two modes. `ignore` starts anyway and leaves the changes where they are. `continue` resumes the prompt an interrupted coder left behind in the `[^]` status, keeping its half-finished changes in place; it expects **exactly one** `[^]` prompt and fails when it finds none or more than one. Only that first round runs on the dirty tree, every later round expects a clean one again, and `continue` cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree would leave the uncommitted changes behind.\n-   Prompt status attribution — a prompt one harness started and another one continued records them in chronological order, as `` by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` ``, in its `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status line alike. Every later continuation appends another `interrupted, continued by …` report instead of dropping an earlier harness.\n-   `--order <from-earliest|from-latest|random>` — `verify` only; order in which the prompt files are walked through. `from-earliest` (the default) starts with the oldest prompt file, `from-latest` starts with the newest one, and `random` shuffles the queue for every pass.\n-   `--commit`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git synchronization of `init`, `add`, `generate-boilerplates` and `verify`, which never touch git unless these flags are used. `--auto-pull` pulls before the command changes anything, `--commit` commits the resulting changes with the coding-agent git identity, and `--auto-push` (which requires `--commit`) pushes the created commit. For `verify` the synchronization is applied around each single verification instead of once per run.\n-   Every commit `ptbk coder` creates contains **only the files of the operation which created it** — the added prompt file for `add`, the archived or repaired prompt file for `verify`, the prompt file together with the files the coding agent has changed for `run` and `server`. Changes which were already in the working tree before the command started are left there, so an unrelated work in progress is never swept into a coder commit.\n-   `--isolate` — `run` only; implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree (`.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>`) with its own copy of `.env`. A verified task is merged back into the current branch as one commit and the worktree is deleted; a task that cannot be merged is marked `[!]`, the failure is committed, and its worktree is kept for a manual merge while the coder continues. Because the worktree nests the whole repository one level deeper, git long path support is enabled for the isolated run so that Windows `MAX_PATH` does not break the checkout. Cannot be combined with `--no-commit`.\n-   `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-error <duration>` — wall-clock pacing; durations like `1h`, `30m`, `5s`; pause and computer sleep count against the wait; `S` skips whatever the coder waits for while `S Skip current waiting` is offered, which besides these three waits covers the harness session-limit wait and the `server` keep-alive poll; errors retry up to 3 times (default wait `10m`).\n-   `--no-ui`, `--preserve-logs` — plain streaming output / keep temp artifacts.\n-   `--port <port>` — `server` only; kanban UI port, default `4441`.\n\nEnvironment variables that may be mentioned: `CODING_AGENT_GIT_NAME`, `CODING_AGENT_GIT_EMAIL`, `CODING_AGENT_GIT_SIGNING_KEY` (agent git identity, created by `ptbk coder init` in `.env`), and `PTBK_HARNESS` / `PTBK_MODEL` / `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` as defaults for the corresponding options.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":34,"oldLines":7,"newStart":34,"newLines":7,"lines":[" -   `--model <model>` — model passed to the harness; **required** for `openai-codex`, `gemini`, and `qwen-code` when they execute prompts, and an optional filter for `list`. --test-before yes-and-fix`                                                                                                                       | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md) sample commands are defined in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md); per-feature snippets in [`../sections/advanced-features.md`](../sections/advanced-features.md).\n\n## Option reference (context for copywriting)\n\nThese `ptbk coder` options may be referenced in page prose and must be described accurately:\n\n-   `--harness <name>` — selects the coding agent; one of the harnesses in [`harness-catalog.md`](./harness-catalog.md). Required when `run` or `server` executes prompts, and an optional filter for `list`.\n-   `--model <model>` — model passed to the harness; **required** for `openai-codex`, `gemini`, and `qwen-code` when they execute prompts, and an optional filter for `list`. The value `default` asks for the default model of that harness; for `openai-codex` it passes no model to Codex at all, so Codex keeps the model of its own configuration — the only thing a ChatGPT-account login accepts.\n-   Prompt routing — add one or more backtick-delimited model, model-family, harness, or selected-agent references to a ready `[ ]` status line, for example `` [ ] use model `gpt-5.5` `` or `` [ ] use agent `developer` ``. The prompt runs when any token matches after normalization, while `!` markers can appear before or after a token. A selected Book agent matches by its configured path (`agents/coding/developer.book`), filename (`developer.book`), filename without `.book` (`developer`), or title from the Book's first line (`Developer Foo bar`).\n-   `ptbk coder list` — list all ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority groups without starting a harness or changing files. Optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--agent`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and `--max-priority` filters preview the queue a selected runner would receive.\n-   Prompt statuses — `[-]` or `[.]` not ready, `[ ]` ready, `[^]` being implemented right now, `[x]` implemented, verified and committed, `[!]` failed. A prompt with no status checkbox is also ready at priority `0`; when processing begins, its new `[^]` line is added before the prompt content. Put `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown file to ignore that entire file. `run` and `server` rewrite `[^]` before every step of a round, so it names the harness, the model, the finished steps and the running one (for example `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress ``). A run started with `--agent` names that agent in front of its harness, as `` [^] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` … ``. Only the final `[x]` is committed, and `[^]` is never reverted, so a killed or crashed coder leaves it behind as the signal that the task was left in the middle; such a prompt is not picked up again automatically.\n-   `--thinking-level <level>` — reasoning effort for supported harnesses: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`.\n-   `--agent <path.book>` — a `.book` file whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt and whose path, filename, filename without `.book`, and Book title can route agent-specific prompts. It also filters `ptbk coder list` without starting a harness.\n-   `--context <text-or-file>` — extra instructions inline or from a project file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`).\n-   `--test <command...>` — verification command run after each prompt; failures are fed back and retried.\n-   `--test-before <no|yes-and-fail|yes-and-fix>` — run the test command before coding; stop on pre-existing failures or create one repair prompt, and use `npm test` when no `--test` command is provided.\n-   `--dry-run` — print unwritten prompts without executing.\n-   `ptbk coder ping` — send one tiny dummy prompt to the harness and model selected with `--harness`, `--model` and `--thinking-level` and report the answer, the response time and the reported usage. It runs no coding task or commit; when the selected harness has missing local ignore rules, it asks before adding them to `.gitignore`. `--allow-credits` and `--no-ui` behave as for `run`, where `--no-ui` streams the raw harness output instead of the compact result.\n-   `--period <duration>` — `ping` only; instead of pinging once, keep pinging once per period until the process is stopped with `CTRL+C`. The duration uses the same format as the `--wait-*` options (`5h`, `30m`, `1h30m`) and must be positive. The period is measured from the start of one ping to the start of the next one, so `--period 5h` really pings every 5 hours regardless of how long a ping takes, and a failed ping is reported without ending the loop. Its main use is keeping the 5-hour quota window of Claude Code permanently open for the price of a few tokens per ping.\n-   `--min-priority <n>`, `--max-priority <n>` — for `run`, process only prompts within the inclusive priority range; for `list`, show only prompts within that range; `--priority <n>` remains an alias for `--min-priority`; for `add`, `--priority <n>` sets the priority of the new prompt (rendered as trailing `!` markers).\n-   `--limit <n>` — stop after N prompt runs (`run` only).\n-   `--count <n>` / `--count <n>*<m>` — `generate-boilerplates` only; number of generated prompt files, optionally with the number of prompts written into each of them. `--count N` is the same as `--count N*1`, the default is `5*1`, and more than one prompt per file is an advanced option: each of the `M` prompts is a separate task, separated by a `---` line, and shares the file's fresh emoji tag.\n-   `--no-auto` — wait for user confirmation before each prompt. Cannot be combined with `--no-questions`, which forbids the very confirmation it waits for.\n-   `--no-questions` — never ask an interactive question, taken by `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server`. Every optional step which needs an answer is skipped and reported together with the command which does it manually: installing a missing coding harness, updating an outdated harness, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing harness ignore rules to `.gitignore`. Because an outdated harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, the npm latest-version lookup is skipped as well, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it.\n-   `--no-commit`, `--git-changes <mode>`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git behavior switches of `run` and `server`, which commit every successful round by default.\n-   `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` — what happens when the working tree has uncommitted changes before a prompt starts. `fail` (the default) refuses to start and asks for a commit, a stash or one of the other two modes. `ignore` starts anyway and leaves the changes where they are. `continue` resumes the prompt an interrupted coder left behind in the `[^]` status, keeping its half-finished changes in place; it expects **exactly one** `[^]` prompt and fails when it finds none or more than one. Only that first round runs on the dirty tree, every later round expects a clean one again, and `continue` cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree would leave the uncommitted changes behind.\n-   Prompt status attribution — a prompt one harness started and another one continued records them in chronological order, as `` by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` ``, in its `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status line alike. Every later continuation appends another `interrupted, continued by …` report instead of dropping an earlier harness.\n-   `--order <from-earliest|from-latest|random>` — `verify` only; order in which the prompt files are walked through. `from-earliest` (the default) starts with the oldest prompt file, `from-latest` starts with the newest one, and `random` shuffles the queue for every pass.\n-   `--commit`, `--auto-push`, `--auto-pull` — git synchronization of `init`, `add`, `generate-boilerplates` and `verify`, which never touch git unless these flags are used. `--auto-pull` pulls before the command changes anything, `--commit` commits the resulting changes with the coding-agent git identity, and `--auto-push` (which requires `--commit`) pushes the created commit. For `verify` the synchronization is applied around each single verification instead of once per run.\n-   Every commit `ptbk coder` creates contains **only the files of the operation which created it** — the added prompt file for `add`, the archived or repaired prompt file for `verify`, the prompt file together with the files the coding agent has changed for `run` and `server`. Changes which were already in the working tree before the command started are left there, so an unrelated work in progress is never swept into a coder commit.\n-   `--isolate` — `run` only; implement each prompt in its own temporary git worktree (`.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>`) with its own copy of `.env`. A verified task is merged back into the current branch as one commit and the worktree is deleted; a task that cannot be merged is marked `[!]`, the failure is committed, and its worktree is kept for a manual merge while the coder continues. Because the worktree nests the whole repository one level deeper, git long path support is enabled for the isolated run so that Windows `MAX_PATH` does not break the checkout. Cannot be combined with `--no-commit`.\n-   `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-error <duration>` — wall-clock pacing; durations like `1h`, `30m`, `5s`; pause and computer sleep count against the wait; `S` skips whatever the coder waits for while `S Skip current waiting` is offered, which besides these three waits covers the harness session-limit wait and the `server` keep-alive poll; errors retry up to 3 times (default wait `10m`).\n-   `--no-ui`, `--preserve-logs` — plain streaming output / keep temp artifacts.\n-   `--port <port>` — `server` only; kanban UI port, default `4441`.\n\nEnvironment variables that may be mentioned: `CODING_AGENT_GIT_NAME`, `CODING_AGENT_GIT_EMAIL`, `CODING_AGENT_GIT_SIGNING_KEY` (agent git identity, created by `ptbk coder init` in `.env`), and `PTBK_HARNESS` / `PTBK_MODEL` / `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` as defaults for the corresponding options.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":36,"oldLines":7,"newStart":36,"newLines":7,"lines":[" -   `ptbk coder list` — list all ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority groups without starting a harness or changing files. a dark mode toggle to the settings page\"`                                                                                                                                         | [Quickstart step           | `ptbk coder list`                               | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `TEST_BEFORE_FIX_COMMAND`       | `ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --test npm test --test-before yes-and-fix`                                                                                                                       | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `GIT_CHANGES_CONTINUE_COMMAND`  | `ptbk coder run --harness claude-code --git-changes continue` --dry-run`                                                                                                                                                                             | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `PING_COMMAND`                  | `ptbk coder ping --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.6-sol --thinking-level xhigh`                                                                                                                    | [Advanced features](../sections/advanced-features.md)                       |\n| `PING_PERIOD_COMMAND`           | `ptbk coder ping --harness claude-code --model claude-sonnet-5 --thinking-level low --period 5h`
