Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers. For example `/agents/doQMRg82izNfJa/chat`, `/agents/doqmrg82iznfja/chat`, and `/agents/DOQMRG82IZNFJA/chat` now all open the same agent and redirect to its canonical id. Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers.\n\n-   Made the standalone VPS Agents Server manage its Let's Encrypt certificates automatically for every assigned domain, whether the domain belongs to the server or to a project. A new process-wide certificate scheduler periodically runs a lightweight `install.sh apply-certificates` maintenance pass that reuses the existing idempotent per-domain certificate configuration: it obtains a certificate for any domain that still lacks one and renews any certificate close to expiry, then re-renders nginx so freshly issued certificates start serving HTTPS. This means a server created **before** its DNS is configured now gets its certificate on its own once the DNS starts resolving — no manual `apply-domains` rerun needed — and expiring certificates are renewed without intervention. The maintenance pass never restarts the Agents Server, never touches the firewall, and keeps every domain isolated in its own certificate lineage, so a single domain failing to validate (or a project failing to run) can never take the main server domain offline; the raw-IP default server and plain-HTTP fallback keep the server reachable from the web throughout. The failed-issuance warning now points operators at the automatic retry (and the immediate `install.sh apply-certificates` command).\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` **All** history view so tasks are ordered by finished time, with the newest finished task on top. The `All` view previously ordered rows by last-update time, which let a self-update that finished long ago sit above chat completions that finished more recently. The default `All` ordering now reuses the shared task timeline timestamp (which resolves to `finishedAt` for terminal tasks) in both the SQLite comparator and the PostgreSQL `ORDER BY`, while still-active tasks keep their start/queue placement instead of dropping to the bottom.\n\n-   Moved the standalone VPS Agents Server installer from `other/vps/install.sh` to `install.sh` in the repository root so the entry-point script is easy to find, while its dependency scripts (for example `other/vps/test-nginx-config-generation.sh`) stay under `other/vps/` and are called relative to the root installer. The self-update flow, the installer self-references it persists into `PTBK_VPS_INSTALL_SCRIPT`, the Agents Server installer-path resolver, and the documented `curl … | bash` deploy instructions now point at the root `install.sh`; the resolver still falls back across candidate paths, so servers self-updating from an older release keep working across the move.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat feedback stars so unpicked stars no longer stay yellow. The shared chat feedback controls now render CSS-colored star icons with their resolved color, fill, and stroke state applied through shared CSS variables and inline SVG icon styles instead of the native colored emoji glyph, inactive stars are hollow even when generic SVG styles are present, and the compact response control plus rating modal share the same rating-message key resolution so both reflect the picked rating consistently.\n\n-   Added `--env` to the standalone VPS Agents Server installer. Fresh installs now default to the `preview` environment, while `--env live`, `--env production`, and `--env lts` select the corresponding Promptbook branch and persist it as `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`.\n\n-   Fixed the standalone VPS Agents Server installer so `curl ... | bash -s -- ...` works under `set -u`. Bash leaves `BASH_SOURCE` empty when executing a script from stdin, so the installer entrypoint now uses a dedicated sourced-script detector and the self-update script-copy step skips the stable-copy rerun when the running installer has no readable file path. The root verification setup now also resolves the same local Agents Server aliases, keeps the CLI build-command unit test mocked at the direct helper import paths, and raises the shared Agents Server production build heap limit after verification exposed a 4 GiB Next build OOM.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server multi-server isolation so servers hosted on one VPS can no longer leak agents, projects, metadata, users, chats, or any other server-scoped data into each other. Each registered server now has **its own SQLite database file** (`servers/<server-namespace>.sqlite` next to the existing database), and one **VPS-wide SQLite registry database** (the existing `agents-server.sqlite`) owned by the super-admin holds only the `_Server` list of servers. The SQLite Supabase-shaped adapter routes every table access through a single choke point — VPS-level `_`-prefixed tables go to the registry database while server-prefixed tables go to the owning server's database under clean unprefixed names — so all existing data access code works unchanged. `/admin/servers` create/rename/delete now manages persistent registry rows with stable ids (renaming a domain keeps the server's data; deleting a registration keeps its database file on disk), the `SERVERS` environment variable remains only a projection for nginx/certbot provisioning and Edge middleware host matching, and creating a server no longer overwrites the shared `SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX` (the root cause of servers flipping into one another's tables). Domains listed in `SERVERS` are auto-registered into the registry on first boot, so a freshly installed VPS bootstraps itself, and the embedded database admin now targets the current server's isolated database only.\n\n-   Added a **Cancel all active tasks** action to the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager`. A guarded button in the background-tasks header requests cancellation of every active (queued + running) durable chat task across all users in one confirmed, reason-required step via a new `/api/admin/chat-tasks/cancel-all` endpoint, reusing the existing single-task cancellation flow for each task and reporting how many tasks were matched and cancelled.\n\n-   Separated the Agents Server `/admin/chat-history` by chat thread instead of one mixed pile. A new **Chat thread** filter (grouped from `chatId` by a new `/api/chat-history/threads` endpoint) narrows the table view to a single conversation once an agent is picked, and the CSV export honors it. The chat transcript view now lists recorded threads and opens one conversation at a time (never mixing threads) and always renders in bubble mode regardless of the article-mode control-panel preference. The table message column now renders Markdown, and links into chat history (super-admin external-chat banner and admin conversation search results) now deep-link to the most detailed view — the recorded conversation in chat view — when the agent and thread are known.\n\n-   Added sortable column headers to Agents Server administration tables, with shared sorting controls and helpers reused across task manager, chat history, chat feedback, messages, files, images, API tokens, metadata, servers, environment variables, usage detail, Shibboleth, and resource monitor tables. Paginated admin lists now send whitelisted sort fields to their loaders so the full result set is ordered before pagination.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard desktop rail so the left panel scrolls independently on short viewports, keeping the stepper and progress controls reachable while preserving the existing fullscreen layout.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard so the right content panel scrolls independently inside the fullscreen layout, keeping long Book, knowledge, and test steps reachable without moving the desktop rail.\n\n-   Added a classic Book editor exit from the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard. A small Book button in the manGo rail now opens the existing classic editor with the current partially created draft, including the generated book text and ready knowledge sources, so users can finish creation outside the manGo flow.\n\n-   Added **Download .book** to the Agents Server agent context menu. The action downloads the stored source book for the selected authenticated local agent using the same safe filename sanitization as book ZIP exports, while the existing inherited-source `/api/book` route remains unchanged.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server chat source chips so JSON-like and binary image citations no longer show raw payload text. Source labels now fall back to compact URL snippets when a source URL is known, or type labels such as `JSON file` and `JPEG image` when it is not; source chips now use semantic SVG icons for websites, JSON, documents, media, archives, and related file types, with URL-backed image citations rendered as thumbnails.\n\n-   Extended runnable Agents Server agent projects with durable public runtime exposure. Project pages and the internal agent-project runtime API can now start dev or static project runtimes, the server persists assigned ports and project subdomains, production Linux runtimes are started as dedicated pm2 processes, and the standalone VPS installer reads the managed project-domain list to configure nginx reverse proxying and SSL certificates. `/admin/servers` now shows project subdomains assigned below each server domain.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates so newly required host software is installed through the same shared dependency path as fresh installs. The code-server installer now uses the standalone release installer instead of global npm installation, avoiding the `Please pass --unsafe-perm to npm to install code-server` failure during `/admin/update`.\n\n-   Added super-admin browser VS Code access for Agents Server agent projects. Project pages now show an **Open VS Code** action and support the GitHub-style `.` shortcut for super admins, launching a per-project `code-server` session rooted at the project directory with matching light/dark theme settings, editable files, git tooling, and terminal CWD on the project root. Standalone VPS installs now install `code-server`, proxy VS Code sessions through an authenticated nginx subpath, route `install.sh` on already installed servers into self-update, and share dependency installation between fresh installs and self-updates so new server-side software dependencies are applied during updates.\n\n-   Added runnable local agent projects to the Agents Server. Local agents can now ask the server for a tracked free port, start a server-owned project dev command, or start a static file server for plain project folders; the prompt instructions expose the internal runtime API through environment variables instead of embedding secrets. Project runtime ports now appear in `/admin/resource-monitor` with links to the live port and owning project plus terminate/release controls, and each project page shows whether its project is running or has an assigned port with the same terminate/release action.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar preview so the sample now renders the existing shared `AsciiOctopus` canvas avatar directly, matching the web avatar visual instead of the blocky terminal rasterization.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar alignment so the web sample now centers the shared animated `AsciiOctopus` lines to the same dashboard width as the surrounding live-terminal boxes.\n\n-   Added persistent per-agent browser profiles to the Agents Server. Every agent now browses in its own isolated Playwright profile (persistent Chromium user-data directory), so cookies, session tokens, logged-in sessions, and other browser data survive across chats and server restarts — for example an agent signed into a social network stays signed in without the user logging in again. The `run_browser` tool resolves the acting agent from the hidden tool runtime context, and the live browser preview (opened from knowledge/citation chips in chat) now runs on the same agent profile via a new `agent` query parameter of `/api/page-preview/stream` threaded through a new optional `agentIdentifier` prop of `<Chat/>`, so when the user logs in somewhere inside the live session the login is saved into the agent's profile for future agent browsing. The profile is managed through the wallet: a new agent-scoped `BROWSER_PROFILE` wallet record type (added by a backwards-compatible migration) stores only the link to the profile directory on the filesystem (default under `.promptbook/agents-server/browser/profiles`, overridable via `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE_STORAGE_DIRECTORY`), it is registered automatically on first agent browsing and editable at `/system/user-wallet`. `BrowserConnectionProvider` now caches one browser context per profile directory and closes contexts with no open pages after an idle timeout (`RUN_BROWSER_CONTEXT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 10 minutes) — the browser is not kept alive while unused, only the profile data stays permanent. The wallet UI and menu are now labeled **Agent Wallet** (records belong to agents, each agent has its own wallet; the `/system/user-wallet` route is kept for backwards compatibility).\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server live browser preview (shown when a cited page cannot be embedded as an iframe) into a remote-desktop-like session inspired by Chrome Remote Desktop and AnyDesk. The preview now forwards natural browser interactions to the server-side headless browser — hovering, clicking, double-clicking (click counts are tracked client-side like in remote desktop viewers), dragging and text selection via raw pointer presses and releases, mouse-wheel scrolling, and full keyboard typing including shortcuts (keys outside the US layout fall back to text insertion). A browser-like toolbar adds back/forward/reload, an editable address bar (submitted URLs are SSRF-checked server-side), local zoom (Ctrl+wheel, pinch, or toolbar buttons, 50–300 %), an \"Open in new tab\" link, and a full screen mode. The remote viewport is sized dynamically: it follows the measured preview area and full screen changes instead of the previous fixed 1280x800. Stream frames are now sourced from a CDP `Page.startScreencast` — pushed on every repaint for smooth video playback and scrolling, idle-cheap, capped at ~15 fps, with a heartbeat that re-sends the last frame so proxies do not drop quiet streams — while the previous screenshot-polling loop remains as a fallback. The input protocol (`src/book-components/Chat/Chat/pagePreview/`) is shared between the new `<LiveBrowserPreview/>` component and the `/api/page-preview/input` route, events are delivered strictly in order with move/wheel coalescing, a new `/api/page-preview/state` route keeps the toolbar in sync with navigations happening inside the page, and a reconnect overlay appears when the stream drops.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder` artificial waits so they are tied to wall-clock deadlines instead of decrementing only while the Node process is actively awake. `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-after-error`, OpenAI Codex rate-limit backoff, and Claude Code session-limit resurrection waits now elapse during `p`/web-UI pauses and while the computer sleeps.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/harness-auth` so the page no longer shows multiple xterm panels. Harness status and apply output now render as plain text, and the **Live authentication terminal** is the only interactive terminal, mounted only while an authentication session is running.\n\n-   Renamed Agents Server standalone VPS harness authentication to `/admin/harness-auth`, with Harness Auth menu/page/API copy and installer guidance aligned around `PTBK_HARNESS` subscription-backed CLI sign-in.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar so the sample now uses the shared terminal avatar renderer and the same `AsciiOctopus` fallback as the real Promptbook Developer coder agent. The terminal avatar dimensions and refresh cadence are centralized in `src/utils/agents/terminalAgentAvatarVisual`, with both the real rich CLI UI and the landing page using that shared preset.\n\n-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so it preserves imports from modules mocked in the same test file. The repair pass now detects static `jest.mock(...)` and `vi.mock(...)` module specifiers and leaves matching imports on their mocked facade module instead of redirecting them to deeper implementation files, preventing repaired imports from bypassing test mocks.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` self-update rows so a successful standalone VPS self-update is no longer shown as failed when the old server process is stopped before the installer writes its final `STATUS=succeeded`. Task-manager self-update snapshots now reuse the same restart-aware target-commit reconciliation as `/admin/update`, and the archived self-update task history stores that resolved success state before a later update overwrites the singleton status file.\n\n-   Updated the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal so it now plays a one-shot `ptbk coder run` sample that mirrors the real rich CLI dashboard: typed command, shared animated agent visual rendered as colored terminal text, `Session` / `Current task` / `Live output` / `Controls` boxes, and final output without blinking, clearing, or looping. The terminal avatar now uses the shared avatar-to-ASCII rendering pipeline instead of a landing-only drawing.\n\n-   Added the `ptbk coder` landing page app at `apps/coder-landing` (http://localhost:4025/). The dark-mode, mobile-friendly Next.js page introduces `ptbk coder` to developers who know Claude Code or OpenAI Codex: copyable syntax-highlighted terminal samples walk from `npm install ptbk` through `ptbk coder init` to the kanban `ptbk coder server`, an animated fake terminal replays a scripted coding session, the `--agent agents/developer.book` option is demonstrated with the default developer agent in a readonly `<BookEditor/>`, and all six harnesses (`claude-code`, `openai-codex`, `github-copilot`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cline`) are presented as cards with logos, model examples, and shell samples. The footer mirrors https://www.ptbk.io/en and states that `ptbk coder` is a Promptbook subproduct by AI Web s.r.o. The app follows the official Promptbook branding and ships with an `apps/coder-landing/specs/` folder of interlinked markdown specs which serve as the single source of truth for 1:1 replication of the page.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server chat source chip for attached images so it shows the original filename (for example `DSC_0139 (2).JPG`) instead of unreadable binary content. Attached files are cited by their content-addressed CDN URL, whose filename is normalized, so the shared citation-label resolver used to download the image and print its first decoded line. Both the durable and private-mode chat surfaces now wrap the resolver with `createAttachmentAwareCitationLabelResolver`, which maps a citation whose URL points to one of the chat attachments back to that attachment's original `name` and only otherwise delegates to the server metadata resolver — which also avoids the needless image download.\n\n-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so cross-boundary imports from `src` to `apps/agents-server/src` can be repaired. The shared project entity scanner can now include app source exports when requested, which lets the repair script resolve Agents Server constants such as `DEFAULT_LOCAL_AGENT_RUNNER_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS` without broadening the files it rewrites.\n\n-   Added automatic standalone VPS self-updates for the Agents Server. `/admin/update` now exposes `.env`-backed automatic update settings for `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED`, `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`, and `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_CRON` (default `0 0 * * *`) while reusing the shared VPS environment writer used by `/admin/environment`. A Node-runtime scheduler checks the configured branch on the cron cadence and starts the existing zero-downtime self-update flow only when the remote branch is ahead. Persisted self-update jobs now record whether they were started manually or automatically, and both `/admin/update` and `/admin/task-manager` show that trigger.\n\n-   Refactored `ptbk agent-folder run-multiple` so `runMultipleAgentMessages` is now a small watch-loop orchestrator. Active queued-message scheduling, local project summary loading, GitHub repository synchronization, idle auto-pull state, shared dashboard presentation, and path/wait helpers now live in focused private modules under `runMultipleAgentMessages/`, while the exported API, queue selection behavior, retry handling, auto-clone/auto-pull timing, console output, and rich UI state remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS self-update utility so `vpsSelfUpdate` is now a small facade. Environment resolution, `.env`/origin configuration, status/log-file persistence, background process launch, overview assembly, git repository reads, candidate commit listing, and stale-job reconciliation now live in focused private modules under `vpsSelfUpdate/`. The exported API, installer invocation, persisted status/log format, update overview payload, and custom commit picker behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat image attachments so clicking an attached image opens an in-chat popup preview instead of navigating to a new browser tab. Non-image attachments still keep the existing new-tab file link behavior.\n\n-   Added `?messageDraft=` quick buttons to Agents Server chat messages alongside the existing `?message=` buttons. A `[Label](?message=...)` button still sends its text immediately, while a new `[Label](?messageDraft=...)` button prefills the composer with an editable draft — focusing the input and moving the caret to the end — so the text can be reviewed and changed before sending. The markdown button parser now recognizes the `messageDraft` link, `<Chat/>` owns the composer prefill through a new internal draft channel (overridable via the new `onQuickMessageDraftButton` prop), and draft buttons are only shown when there is a composer (or handler) to receive the draft.\n\n-   Fixed the `ptbk coder run` rich terminal UI so sessions started with `--limit <run-count>` now show that configured run limit in the Session scope summary.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server Shibboleth authentication utility so `shibbolethAuthentication` is now a small facade. The SAML protocol/user constants, shared type contracts, RelayState sanitization and request-detail extraction, configuration resolution (Service Provider URL derivation and Identity Provider metadata fetching and XML parsing), Node-SAML client and Service Provider metadata generation, SAML profile-attribute extraction, prefixed table-name resolvers, authentication-attempt audit logging, and user/identity linking now live in focused sibling modules under `shibbolethAuthentication/`. The re-exported functions and types, the SAML request/response handling, the emitted Service Provider metadata, and the observable authentication and audit behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server admin task-manager loader so `getAdminChatTasks` is now a small facade. The SQLite-mode fallback path (raw job/timeout row and user/agent lookup loading, record mapping, in-memory view/search filtering, dashboard sorting, and summary counters) and the PostgreSQL raw-SQL path (the shared union query, the list and counters query builders, and SQL row/counter mapping), together with the shared ISO-timestamp helpers and SQL value coercion, now live in focused sibling modules under `getAdminChatTasks/`. The exported `getAdminChatTasks` signature and `GetAdminChatTasksData` type, the SQLite/PostgreSQL dispatch, the emitted SQL, and the observable task items, counters, and pagination remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server server backup ZIP builder so `createServerBackupZipStream` is now a small facade. The shared lazy-loading Supabase context and table loaders, the section dispatcher and per-section exporters (metadata, agents, conversations, users, files, and messages), the manifest builder, the user/agent preview maps, attachment reference indexing, feedback-thread parsing, wallet redaction, binary download, filename generation, and the generic row/value utilities now live in focused sibling modules under `serverBackup/`. The exported `createServerBackupZipStream` signature, the archive layout, the `promptbook-server-backup/v2` manifest, and the observable ZIP contents remain unchanged.\n\n-   Added `--limit <candidate-count>` to `ptbk coder find-refactor-candidates`, so a single run creates at most that many refactor prompts and, when more candidates are found, keeps only the most important ones. Importance is a combined severity score — the sum of `actual / threshold` ratios across every exceeded line-count, entity-count, function-count, and complexity threshold — computed while scanning, so files that overshoot more thresholds (or overshoot them further) are preferred. The limit is applied after skipping candidates that already have prompts and can be combined with `--level`. The positive-integer option parser previously private to `ptbk coder run` was extracted into a shared `createPositiveIntegerOptionParser` reused by both commands, and the VS Code \"Find refactor candidates for Coding Agent\" terminal now passes `--limit 10`.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server local SQLite Supabase adapter so `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase` is now a small facade. The table-schema metadata and resolvers, value serialization/deserialization, mutation payload defaults, PostgREST filter translation, table/index DDL, row-level DML, SQLite error normalization, low-level SQL helpers, and the Supabase-shaped client/table/query-builder classes now live in focused sibling modules under `localSqliteSupabase/`. The public `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase`, `$resetLocalSqliteSupabaseForTests`, and `ensureLocalSqliteTableReadIndexes` exports, the generated SQL, and the observable query behavior remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server mocked-chats editor state so `useMockedChatsEditorState` is now a lean state orchestrator. Preset cloning, saved-list lookup/upsert/dirty comparison, list persistence and error resolution, delete confirmation, draft save-flow factories, and the participant/message/settings draft reducers now live in focused sibling modules. The API calls, request payloads, feedback messages, draft mutation behavior, and the `UseMockedChatsEditorState` contract remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server export-as-transpiled-code page client so `AgentCodePageClient` is now a small page orchestrator. Transpiler listing, code generation, ZIP download, and agent-profile loading moved behind a focused `useAgentCodeExportState` hook, while the header, source-book viewer, transpiler picker/harness section, export warnings, error banners, and generated-code preview are now separate presentational components. The API calls, request payloads, abort/cleanup behavior, error/loading states, and visible UI remain unchanged.\n\n-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS update client so `/admin/update` now separates overview polling, target environment controls, current deployment metrics, pending commits, and update-job log/status rendering into focused private helpers. The update POST payloads, polling behavior, success/error messages, and visible UI behavior remain unchanged while the top-level `<UpdateClient/>` is now a small page orchestrator.\n\n-   Enhanced Agents Server chat dictation with a failover-backed speech-to-text flow and Wispr Flow-inspired correction loop. The chat input now keeps microphone states clear through start, stop, processing, permission, and error transitions; preserves the original selection for replace-selection dictation; keeps interim transcript text outside the textarea so the caret stays stable; lets corrections update the local custom-word dictionary including capitalization-only fixes; and backtracks only the tracked dictated chunk instead of restoring the whole previous composer value. The provider layer now reports terminal stall failures when no fallback remains, while the existing OpenAI transcription provider and Browser Web Speech fallback stay behind the shared speech-to-text provider abstraction.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server homepage graph layout so server, folder, and agent subsets are placed by a deterministic free layout instead of nested grids. The current server is now centered in the graph, folders and agents keep their React Flow parent boundaries, and inheritance/import/team links are used as layout hints at the server, folder, and agent levels so relationship arrows can pass cleanly through the subset boundaries without flattening the hierarchy.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so attached files are visible to the answering agent. Runner `.book` files now include the existing chat attachment context for user messages, preserving image/file URLs and best-effort inline text previews for readable attachments before the local or git-backed runner writes the final answer.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server agent inheritance so local parent agents are loaded directly from the server collection instead of re-entering the authenticated `/api/book` HTTP route. `FROM @Basic` / `FROM {Basic}` now materializes the referenced local parent, agents without `FROM` inherit from the local Adam agent, and `FROM @Void` / `FROM {Void}` still explicitly disables inheritance.\n\n-   Added security PRDs for current Agents Server risks that still need implementation: unauthenticated browser-test automation APIs, missing owner-scoped private agent/folder authorization, and unauthenticated CDN uploads.\n\n-   Leveraged the `spaceTrim` utility for authored multiline strings that were still assembled via array `.join('\\n')` or `+ '\\n\\n' +` concatenation. The `TEAM` commitment's shared teammate-usage guidance, the built-in `ptbk coder` boilerplate template contents, and the `<LlmChatPreview/>` fallback scenario greeting now use `spaceTrim` template literals — producing byte-identical output while improving readability. The now-unused `buildCoderPromptTemplateContent` helper was removed.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk -v` so it prints the Promptbook version just like `ptbk --version`, while keeping `-v` / `--verbose` available for subcommands that use verbose logging. Added VS Code terminal shortcuts for both version checks.\n\n-   Replaced frozen citation page-preview screenshots in Agents Server chat with live browser previews for sources that cannot be embedded in an iframe. The shared `<CitationIframePreview/>` now opens a Playwright-backed MJPEG stream through `/api/page-preview/stream`, forwards click and wheel input through `/api/page-preview/input`, and keeps the existing iframe path for embeddable URLs. Active live preview sessions are tracked in process memory, closed when the modal stream is aborted, and surfaced as `Browser preview` rows in `/admin/task-manager` without a database migration.\n\n-   Surfaced the standalone VPS self-update session triggered from `/admin/update` as a task row inside the Agents Server admin `/admin/task-manager` dashboard. The task-manager API now reads the persisted self-update job snapshot via a new lightweight `readVpsSelfUpdateJobSnapshot` helper (no git access, safe for admin polling), maps it into an `AdminChatTaskRecord` of the new `VPS_SELF_UPDATE` kind through the shared `mapVpsSelfUpdateJobToAdminChatTask` utility, and prepends the synthetic row to page 1 whenever it matches the requested view/search. The row is labelled \"Self-update\", counts toward the running / failed-24h summary metrics, and hides the row-level Cancel/Retry buttons because the self-update lifecycle is driven from `/admin/update` rather than the durable chat-task admin API.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server footer's \"Made with ❤️ in Europe\" line to show a deterministic positive/neutral emoji derived from the deployment commit hash. The footer now passes the commit-specific emoji through the existing translation placeholder, with a shared `getCommitFooterEmoji` helper and unit coverage for missing SHA fallback, deterministic mapping, and variation across commit hashes.\n-   Changed the Agents Server footer version line to show the latest server release tag, the deployed commit short hash when the server is newer than that tag, and the release age linked to the Git repository. The footer now receives cached server-side Git metadata reused from the self-update helpers, keeping the client footer render lightweight.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so the runner-visible message book for the first durable user turn is assembled through one shared lifecycle helper that prepends the configured `INITIAL MESSAGE` agent greeting and then includes the current `MESSAGE @User` turn. This keeps the synthetic greeting shown in empty chats available to out-of-process runners even though it is not persisted in `UserChat.messages`, while avoiding duplicate local/external thread-building logic.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server initial book seeding so bundled default and `.core` books honor their own `META VISIBILITY` commitment. The standalone seeder and managed-server bootstrap transaction now omit the explicit default visibility override and let the shared persistence normalization resolve the visibility from the book source first, falling back to `UNLISTED` only when the book does not declare it.\n\n-   Hid Agents Server folders whose name starts with `.` (for example `.core`) from the homepage agents list by default, and added a toolbar **Show hidden** / **Hide hidden** toggle so administrators can opt back into seeing them. The new `filterHiddenFolderTree` utility removes hidden folders together with their descendants and the agents inside them in one pass, so the LIST, GRAPH, OFFICE, MAZE, and PIXEL_OFFICE views stay consistent. The toggle state is persisted in the URL as `hidden=show` (mirroring the existing `view=` query pattern) and the toggle button only appears when the unfiltered organization snapshot actually contains a hidden folder, so workspaces without any `.`-prefixed folder are unaffected.\n\n-   Bumped the default coding model used by the `coder:run` npm script created by `ptbk coder init` from `gpt-5.4` to `gpt-5.5`. The bundled `agents/developer.book` (copied into the consumer project from `agents/default/developer.book` via the existing CLI runtime-asset path resolution in `ensureCoderDeveloperAgentFile`) and the automatic post-init boilerplate generation are unchanged; only the `--model` flag baked into the generated script is updated, so `npm run coder:run` now drives OpenAI Codex with `gpt-5.5` by default.\n\n-   Removed the placeholder **\"Working on your request\"** title and the **\"What I'm Doing Now:\"** wrapper from Agents Server durable chat progress cards so the response no longer shows generic headings between the `THINKING_MESSAGES` rotation and the final answer. The phase-based progress card (`createUserChatProgressCard`), the in-process harness progress card (`createUserChatHarnessProgressCard`), and the `agent_progress` tool's default title fallback no longer set the literal `'Working on your request'` heading; the existing `now`/`next`/`items` real-state markdown still renders, with `now` shown directly instead of under a generic label, and the title field stays optional so agents can still supply their own meaningful heading through `agent_progress`.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` TEAM syntax highlighting so inline email addresses like `team@foo.bar` stay plain text while compact teammate references such as `@Paul` and `{Erik Smith}` remain highlighted and linked.\n\n-   Hid non-actionable `{Void}` inheritance and `Time` capability chips from Agents Server homepage agent cards. The underlying agent capabilities and runtime behavior are unchanged; `{Void}` still resolves as an explicit no-parent marker and `USE TIME` still enables time access, but these labels no longer take space in compact card badges.\n\n-   Made standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates more tolerant of intermittent `next-build exited with code null` failures. CLI-owned `ptbk agents-server build` runs now pass a conservative `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_BUILD_WORKER_COUNT=1` into the Agents Server Next config so static analysis/prerender workers do not scale with VPS CPU count while the old pm2 server is still serving traffic. The build wrapper now also retries once when the Next build child is killed by the operating system (for example `SIGKILL` from memory pressure) and reports a branded markdown error with the exit code, signal, and attempt count instead of the vague `code null` message.\n\n-   Sped up Agents Server local chat message handling by allowing the foreground local agent runner to run up to 3 harness instances in parallel by default, exposed as the new `LOCAL_AGENT_RUNNER_MAX_PARALLEL_MESSAGES` setting on `/admin/limits`. The Agents Server launcher now loads this limit together with the local runner retry cap and passes it into `ptbk agent-folder run-multiple`, whose scheduler keeps polling for newly queued files while earlier harness tasks are still running so a fresh message can start without waiting for the previous answer to finish. Local runner queue filenames now include the durable chat job id, preventing concurrent turns in the same chat from overwriting one another, and the server-side local queue mirroring no longer blocks behind an incomplete previous assistant placeholder.\n\n-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-update leaving multiple `promptbook-agents-server-*` pm2 processes online after partial failures (and even after some successful runs). The blue/green `self_update_agents_server` flow in `other/vps/install.sh` only stopped the immediately previous `old_app_name`, so any orphan left behind by an earlier failed run kept restarting forever via pm2's exponential backoff — wasting RAM/CPU and breaking the \"single instance\" invariant required for a clean `pm2 resurrect` after VPS reboot. The installer now ships a `cleanup_orphan_agents_server_pm2_processes` helper that uses `pm2 jlist` to enumerate every process matching `${PTBK_PM2_BASE_APP_NAME}` / `${PTBK_PM2_BASE_APP_NAME}-*` and deletes everything except the one instance currently serving traffic, then calls `pm2 save` so the systemd-managed `pm2 resurrect` boot path persists exactly one Agents Server process. The new helper runs in three places: at the start of `self_update_agents_server` (sweeps orphans left behind by previous failed runs before any new work begins), in the \"already installed\" shortcut (so re-running the same target also converges to one instance), and at the end of the successful self-update path (running right after the existing `stop_pm2_process_if_running \"$old_app_name\"` so any leftover sibling instance is also removed). A new `SELF_UPDATE_ACTIVE_APP_NAME` global tracks the blue/green hand-off so the `write_failed_self_update_status_on_exit` trap can also run the same cleanup — keeping the old instance if nginx had not switched yet, or keeping the new one if nginx had already moved to the replacement port — meaning a failed `/admin/update` no longer leaves pm2 in a multi-instance state either.\n\n-   Added `META VISIBILITY` as the book-language source of truth for Agents Server agent visibility. Agent creation, book saves, menu visibility changes, and management API visibility updates now normalize the commitment to `PRIVATE`, `UNLISTED`, or `PUBLIC` and mirror it into the database column used for filtering. Bundled default agents now declare their visibility in book source, with `Generic chatter` public and the other defaults private.\n\n-   Added `--limit <run-count>` to `ptbk coder run`, letting coding-agent sessions stop cleanly after the configured number of successful prompt runs. The legacy `run-codex-prompts` option parser now accepts the same flag, and the VS Code terminal list includes a prepared Codex/Claude zig-zag script that runs one prompt per harness with `--limit 1`.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server admin user responses so `/api/users`, `/api/users/[username]`, and the Shibboleth admin dashboard no longer expose `passwordHash`. User-facing code now shares an explicit public user projection and `toPublicUser` mapper, while authentication and password-change paths use narrow internal projections only where the hash is needed.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server `/api/emails/incoming/sendgrid` against forged SendGrid Inbound Parse callbacks. The route now reads the raw multipart body first, requires a configured `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_PUBLIC_KEY` (or `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` for HMAC deployments), validates the SendGrid signature headers before `formData()` parsing, rejects stale timestamps outside a 5-minute replay window, and only accepts callbacks delivered through `SENDGRID_INBOUND_PARSE_HOSTS`. Invalid or misconfigured callbacks now fail before `parseInboundSendgridEmail` can turn caller-supplied sender/recipient data into inbound `EMAIL` rows in the `Message` table.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server password authentication against online guessing. `/api/auth/login`, the existing server-action login path, and `/api/auth/change-password` now share a per-process authentication attempt limiter that tracks failed attempts by request IP, username, and `(IP, username)` pair. Repeated failures trigger exponential backoff, excessive failures in the sliding window return `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`, and every failed, successful, and rate-limited password check is logged with the requesting IP for forensics.\n\n-   Hardened Agents Server `/api/chat/export/pdf` against unauthenticated and SSRF-style abuse. The route now requires `getCurrentUser()` before reading the payload, applies a per-user sliding-window rate limit before spawning Playwright, sanitizes generated chat-export HTML URL attributes through the existing `assertSafeUrl` guard before rendering, blocks all Chromium network requests except non-network `about:` / `data:` URLs during PDF generation, and returns `Content-Disposition` with a quoted ASCII fallback plus RFC 5987 `filename*` encoding.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so users see real progress in the requested sequence instead of an immediate synthetic queued card:\n\n    -   Newly queued assistant placeholders no longer persist a progress card, which lets the browser rotate the configured `THINKING_MESSAGES` while the worker has not picked up the job yet.\n    -   When the local or external agent runner actually receives the request, the assistant placeholder now remains on the browser-side `THINKING_MESSAGES` rotation until the final answer is ready.\n    -   The in-process streaming runner path now derives one visible harness update from streamed tool-call snapshots, reusing the same hidden-tool filtering as chat chips so `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` stay internal while real actions surface as **\"Running action: Searching the web.\"** or **\"Action completed: Browsing the web.\"**\n    -   The final answer still replaces the progress surface as before, and progress text summarizes user-facing actions/results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought, raw tool payloads, secrets, or technical logs.\n\n-   Fixed `\\`headers\\` was called outside a request scope`crash during the standalone VPS Agents Server installation. The bundled-default-agents step runs the`seedDefaultAgents.ts`script via`tsx`outside any Next.js request, but`seedCoreAgents`reached for table names through`$getTableName('Agent')` / `$getTableName('AgentFolder')`, which transitively called `$provideServer()` → `next/headers#headers()` and threw on the bare CLI. The two internal helpers (`loadExistingActiveAgentNames` and `ensureCoreFolderExists`) now accept the `tablePrefix` already resolved by `seedCoreAgents` from `options.tablePrefix ?? process.env.SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX ?? ''` and build the prefixed `Agent` / `AgentFolder` table names directly, mirroring the synchronous concatenation pattern used by `AgentCollectionInSupabase.getTableName`. The Next.js-request-scoped `$getTableName`import is dropped from`seedCoreAgents.ts`, so the standalone seeder no longer touches request-scope APIs — request-handling code paths keep using `$getTableName`unchanged. The companion`registerServerErrorSentryLogging.test.ts`\"keeps logging locally when Sentry is not configured\" case is also tightened to clear`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`along with`SENTRY_DSN`(and to restore it in`afterEach`), because `resolveOptionalSentryDsn`falls back to the public DSN — the previous test passed only on machines without a populated`.env`, and the local `npm run test-for-ptbk-coder` verification surfaced it.\n\n-   Removed the unauthenticated infinite-stream DoS endpoint `/api/long-streaming` from Agents Server. The route opened a `ReadableStream` and pushed a single byte every 100 ms inside a `while (just(true))` loop with no termination condition, no `request.signal` abort handling, no authentication, and no rate limit, so any anonymous client could hold one (or many) connections open indefinitely to consume Node's event-loop, HTTP keep-alive slots, and reverse-proxy connection budget on the standalone VPS deployment — a denial-of-service primitive that needed **zero** authentication or skill to exploit. The endpoint was a leftover demo / test route with no caller anywhere in the Agents Server frontend or in the rest of the repository, so deleting the `apps/agents-server/src/app/api/long-streaming/` folder closes the attack surface entirely without removing any real feature.\n\n-   Fixed two internal shared-secret tokens reusing `ADMIN_PASSWORD` and other unrelated secrets in Agents Server. Both `resolveUserChatWorkerInternalToken` (which protects the internal background-worker routes `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run`, `/api/internal/user-chat-timeouts/run`, and `/api/internal/agent-runner-limits`) and `resolveTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` (which authorizes same-server `TEAM` calls into private teammate agents) fell back to a chain of unrelated environment variables when their dedicated `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN` / `PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN` variable was missing. The worker-token chain in particular ended in a publicly-known constant (`'promptbook-user-chat-worker'`), so an operator who deployed without explicitly configuring the variable left the gate effectively open — anyone who computed `sha256('user-chat-worker:promptbook-user-chat-worker')` could drive jobs at will. Even on the \"good\" path, deriving the worker token from `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` or `ADMIN_PASSWORD` meant leaking either secret leaked the worker token and vice versa.\n\n    Both functions now require their dedicated environment variable and never fall back to `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL`, or any hardcoded literal — matching the existing `SESSION_SECRET`, `GITHUB_APP_STATE_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_STATE_SECRET` patterns so all \"must be a dedicated secret\" stories share one approach:\n\n    -   `resolveUserChatWorkerInternalToken` caches the value resolved from `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN` on first use. In production it throws a clear `EnvironmentMismatchError` (with the same `spaceTrim` markdown format as the existing `SESSION_SECRET` guard) instead of silently using a shared credential, and outside production it generates a per-process random token via `crypto.randomBytes(32)` and warns once — so local development keeps working without configuration while still rejecting the unsafe fallback chain.\n    -   `resolveTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` now only reads `PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN`; when the variable is missing it returns `null` so the existing `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` and `isTeamInternalAgentAccessToken` guards already in place fail closed — same-server team access is simply disabled and no header is sent (or accepted) instead of silently authorizing requests with the wrong secret.\n    -   Updated the deployment plumbing so a fresh standalone VPS installation does not require manual configuration: `other/vps/install.sh` now calls `ensure_secret_env_value PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_USER_CHAT_WORKER_TOKEN 32` and `ensure_secret_env_value PROMPTBOOK_TEAM_AGENT_ACCESS_TOKEN 32` next to the existing `SESSION_SECRET` generator, so both secrets are auto-provisioned with `openssl rand -hex 32` on first boot and persisted into the installed `.env`. The two new keys were also added to `VPS_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_KEYS` so administrators can rotate them from the VPS UI, to `ptbk agents-server init` so the local scaffold writes documented placeholders, to the root `.env.example`, and to the Agents Server e2e harness so Playwright tests run with dedicated values that differ from the admin password.\n    -   Documented both variables in `apps/agents-server/README.md` next to `SESSION_SECRET` (anchors `agents-server-env-ptbk-agents-server-user-chat-worker-token` and `agents-server-env-promptbook-team-agent-access-token`) and removed the misleading \"If unset, `ADMIN_PASSWORD` will be used as a fallback\" note from `env-manual/GITHUB_APP.md` so the operator-facing docs no longer endorse credential reuse.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server secret and token comparisons. Three additional comparison sites (the signed-session HMAC signature in `parseSessionToken`, the same-server TEAM access token in `isTeamInternalAgentAccessToken`, and the shared internal worker token in the `/api/internal/agent-runner-limits` and `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run` routes) used JavaScript's `===` / `!==` operators, which short-circuit on the first byte that differs and let a remote attacker who can measure response timing recover each secret one byte at a time. All three sites now share a new `isTimingSafeEqualString` utility (in `src/utils/`) that calls Node.js's `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length `Buffer`s and returns `false` immediately on length mismatch (which only leaks length, not content). The helper tolerates `null` / `undefined` inputs so callers can forward raw request values without an extra guard, and the session-cookie comparison stays compatible with legacy tokens because both sides are still derived from the same `HMAC-SHA256` hex digest of equal length.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server `/api/internal/user-chat-jobs/run` looping back-to-back forever when an old `FAILED` local chat job still had its `failed` message-folder book on disk. `synchronizeLocalUserChatJob` was re-marking such jobs as `FAILED` on every tick, which set `didMutate: true` and caused the worker route's `after()` self-requeue to fire immediately. The failed-file branch now mirrors the existing timeout-branch guard (`job.status !== 'FAILED'`), so already-failed jobs short-circuit to `waiting` instead of being re-persisted, and the route stops requeueing itself.\n\n-   Extended standalone VPS Agents Server non-interactive installation:\n\n    -   Added the explicit `--yes-i-understand-that-script-should-be-run-on-fresh-server` installer option alongside `PTBK_CONFIRM_FRESH_VPS=yes`, so automated installs can acknowledge the fresh-server requirement without an interactive prompt.\n    -   Added installer options for the common automated values (`--domain`, `--openai-api-key`, `--sentry-dsn`, and `--admin-password`) while reusing the same defaults and environment variables as the interactive prompts.\n    -   Documented interactive and non-interactive standalone VPS installation examples in the README, including the non-interactive harness skip behavior.\n\n-   Replaced the remote Promptbook Core Agents Server with a bundled local `.core` folder so each Agents Server can run without any external dependency on `core.ptbk.io`:\n\n    -   Removed the `CORE_AGENTS_SERVER` constant from `servers.ts` along with the `CORE_SERVER` and `IS_CORE_SERVER_HIDDEN` metadata defaults; new servers no longer point at a special core federated server and federated servers are now all equal.\n    -   Added a new bundled `.core/` subfolder under `agents/default/` containing the well-known `adam.book` and `teacher.book` (plus other built-in core agents). Default-agent seeding now also seeds these books into a database `.core` folder via the new shared `seedCoreAgents` helper (reused by both the standalone `seedDefaultAgents` runtime path and the managed-server bootstrap transaction through the new `seedServerCoreAgents` companion).\n    -   On every server start (and after every default-agent install), the seeder auto-creates the `.core` folder when missing and inserts any well-known core agent (Adam, Teacher, …) that is not already present, regardless of the visibility set on the bundled book — so Adam is always available as the implicit ancestor for every agent.\n    -   `getWellKnownAgentUrl` now returns the URL of the local well-known agent on the current Agents Server origin (`/agents/adam`, `/agents/teacher`, …) instead of resolving the deprecated `CORE_SERVER` metadata, so `FROM {Adam}`, the Teacher remote agent, and custom-domain Adam fallback all stay inside the current server.\n    -   Removed the now-obsolete `defaultFederatedAgents` background sync (`scheduleDefaultFederatedAgentsSync`, `synchronizeDefaultFederatedAgents`, `fetchCoreOrganizationPayload`, …) that copied default boilerplate agents from `CORE_SERVER` into every new server; the local `.core` seeder fully replaces it.\n    -   `getFederatedServers` no longer special-cases a hidden core server; it just returns the user-configured `FEDERATED_SERVERS` list (empty by default), and the `excludeHiddenCoreServer` option was dropped from its three call sites (homepage layout, federated agents API, federated search provider).\n\n-   Added Agents Server agents import/export on the agents listing:\n\n    -   Admins can download `{server-name}.agents.zip`, containing `.book` files directly in the agents folder structure so importing it into a fresh server recreates the agents and folders.\n    -   Admins can import dropped or selected `.book` files and ZIP archives; ZIP folder structure is embedded under the currently open folder, non-book ZIP entries trigger a proceed warning and are ignored, same-book duplicates are skipped, and different-book duplicate names ask whether to import duplicates or skip conflicts.\n\n-   Added standalone metadata import/export to the Agents Server `/admin/metadata` page:\n\n    -   Admins can now download a `{server-name}.metadata.json` file containing the Promptbook version and only metadata values/notes that differ from built-in defaults.\n    -   Admins can import that JSON into another server; omitted built-in metadata fields resolve to current defaults, so exporting a configured server and importing into a fresh server recreates the metadata configuration without bundling full server data.\n    -   Metadata imports from `/admin/metadata` now ask admins for each imported metadata key whether to keep the current value or use the imported value, and skipped entries preserve the current server configuration instead of resetting omitted built-in defaults.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server `/admin/update` super-admin page so it shows richer context before, during, and after a standalone VPS self-update — making it easier to decide when to update and to debug a failed update:\n\n    -   `readVpsSelfUpdateOverview` now also returns a `pendingCommits` list (subject, short/full commit hash, author timestamp) for the commits between the currently deployed checkout and the latest commit on the configured branch, capped at 100 entries so a long-stale server still responds quickly. A new `<PendingCommitsCard/>` renders that list together with the existing `X commits behind · Y time behind` drift summary, so the admin can review exactly what is about to be installed.\n    -   The overview now performs a best-effort fetch of the tracked remote branch before calculating update drift, then returns the latest remote commit subject/date/hash from the local object database when available. The current and latest commit cards, plus every pending-commit row, now visibly show the commit subject, full hash, and authored date.\n    -   Factored the time-behind suffix out of `buildDeploymentDriftLabel` into a new shared `buildDeploymentTimeBehindLabel` helper so the same localized `N days behind` text powers both the current-deployment card and the pending-commits card without duplication.\n    -   Added a new `GET /api/admin/update/log` route that streams the full persisted `self-update.log` file (gated by `isUserGlobalAdmin`) together with a `Content-Disposition` filename, backed by a new `readVpsSelfUpdateLogFileContent` helper in `vpsSelfUpdate.ts`.\n    -   When the latest update job's status is `failed`, the Update job card now shows **Copy log** and **Download log** buttons that hit the new endpoint and reuse the shared `downloadBlob` / `parseFilenameFromContentDisposition` helpers (same flow as the existing Backup export), so the admin can quickly share the full installer log with the developers for debugging instead of only seeing the truncated terminal tail.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/update` self-update failing on the standalone VPS during the post-compile `Linting and checking validity of types ...` phase with `next-build exited with code null.` (the Node build process was being killed by the OS, typically by the OOM killer, after webpack had already retried minification multiple times). The shared `other/vps/install.sh` `build_agents_server` step now sets `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_IGNORE_NEXT_VALIDATION=true` so the VPS production build skips the duplicate Next.js lint + TypeScript validation step that is already enforced by repository CI, matching the existing CLI materialized-runtime build path and letting the self-update finish reliably on memory-constrained VPS hosts.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server durable chat progress card so each preparation phase shows the **real runtime state** that has actually been resolved so far, instead of a fixed scripted blurb that was identical for every chat turn:\n\n    -   `createUserChatProgressCard` now accepts a `UserChatProgressContext` object and composes the `now`/`next` markdown from real signals — resolved agent name, attachment count, configured tool count and friendly tool labels (e.g. `web browser`, `web search`, `email sending`), knowledge-source count, calendar/email/project integrations, the resolved LLM provider title, and whether the AgentKit runtime came from the in-process cache.\n    -   `createRunUserChatJobExecutionContext` builds that context incrementally as the worker resolves new information and forwards it through `reportProgress` at every phase, so the user sees, for example, **\"Loading the instructions and configured commitments for agent Cooking Coach (2 knowledge sources)\"** instead of the previous static **\"Preparing the agent instructions and context needed for this request.\"**\n    -   The `starting_response` update is now emitted **after** the AgentKit cache lookup completes, so the progress text can name the actual provider (e.g. **\"Calling the language model via OpenAI\"**) and call out whether the agent had to be prepared fresh.\n    -   Added a small `resolveUserChatProgressToolHighlights` helper that maps technical commitment tool identifiers (`web_search`, `useBrowser`, `send_email`, …) to short user-facing labels and excludes the internal `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` tools that should never appear as user-relevant capabilities.\n    -   Updated the queued-message lifecycle copy to reflect the actual queueing state (**\"Your message is waiting in the queue for the next available worker to pick it up.\"**) and updated `userChatMessageLifecycle.test.ts` accordingly.\n\n-   Added a new `Octopus 3D 4` built-in avatar visual as a smoother, blobbier continuation of `Octopus 3D 3`, and promoted it to the new shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`:\n\n    -   Reused the seeded `Octopus3` morphology profile together with the shared projected-eye and projected-mouth helpers so the new proper-3D octopus stays consistent with the rest of the octopus family without duplicating face-rendering logic.\n    -   Rendered the whole octopus as one continuous blobby mesh sampled at a higher latitude/longitude resolution so the silhouette reads as a round, real-octopus body with eight tentacle lobes that smoothly fuse into the mantle instead of attaching as separate ribbons.\n    -   Drove the tentacle motion with a combined primary, secondary, and slow-curl sine harmonic per lobe so the tentacles wave naturally and continuously, like a real octopus drifting in water, while remaining cute and simple.\n    -   Added a richer multi-pass shading pipeline (key light, rim light, soft gloss highlight, seeded pigment spots, and per-patch outline) on top of the existing palette tones, so the silhouette feels textured and visually appealing without leaving the simple flat-stylized look.\n    -   Kept avatar pointer tracking on both the full mesh silhouette and the projected eyes — the head turns toward the mouse cursor more responsively than `Octopus 3D 3` and the eyes track the pointer inside the rotated head.\n    -   Switched the shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL_ID` to `octopus3d4`, updated the Agents Server `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL` metadata default + allowed-values note to include `OCTOPUS3D4`, and added a backwards-compatible database migration that upgrades existing `OCTOPUS3D3` defaults to `OCTOPUS3D4` while preserving any administrator-customized value.\n\n-   Fixed broken access control on chat history, chat feedback, and agent CRUD routes of Agents Server. Multiple route handlers guarded themselves with `getCurrentUser()` (i.e. \"the caller is logged in\") but never checked that the **specific record** being read, modified, or deleted belonged to the caller or that the caller was an administrator, so any authenticated user — including self-registered unprivileged users — could read, mutate, or destroy data that belonged to other users / other agents:\n\n    -   `/api/chat-history` (`GET`/`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/[id]` (`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/export` (`GET`), `/api/chat-feedback` (`GET`/`DELETE`), and `/api/chat-feedback/export` (`GET`) returned (or deleted) the **entire** `ChatHistory` / `ChatFeedback` tables across every agent and user. These endpoints power the admin-only `/admin/chat-history` and `/admin/chat-feedback` screens — which expose IPs, anonymous `userNote`s, and `expectedAnswer`s across all agents — so they are now gated by `isUserAdmin()` instead of `getCurrentUser()`, returning `401 Unauthorized` for non-administrators. The two admin pages and the agent-context-menu entries that link to them were updated to require admin as well, so non-administrators no longer see dead-end links to those screens.\n    -   `PATCH /api/agents/[agentName]` (rename / change visibility) and `DELETE /api/agents/[agentName]` (tombstone) never resolved the agent's owner. Both handlers now resolve the target agent through a new shared `findAgentForCallerWriteAccess` helper that combines `findOwnedAgentByIdentifier` (reusing the same ownership primitive as the v1 management API) with an `isUserAdmin()` admin override, and reject with `404 Not Found` when the agent does not belong to the caller and the caller is not an administrator. The visibility update is now scoped to the resolved row by primary key instead of matching every agent that shares the supplied name or permanent id. The new helper also covers legacy `ADMIN_PASSWORD` administrators that have no database user id.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in three additional Agents Server endpoints that accepted a caller-supplied URL and fetched it server-side without authentication and without the existing `assertSafeUrl` SSRF guard:\n\n    -   `/api/page-preview/screenshot` opened the URL in a headless Playwright browser (which executes JavaScript on the fetched page) and returned a PNG screenshot. The only validation was that the scheme was `http:` or `https:`, so an unauthenticated attacker could screenshot `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (AWS / GCP / Azure metadata service), or any RFC-1918 private address.\n    -   `/api/page-preview/check` performed a server-side `fetch` (HEAD with `redirect: follow`) through `checkIfUrlCanBeEmbedded` with the same lack of validation.\n    -   `/api/team-agent-profile` called `fetchAgentProfile` against any URL that passed the structural `isValidAgentUrl` check and forwarded the internal team access token to the target. The same-origin check inside `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` already prevented the token from leaking to truly cross-origin URLs, but the SSRF itself was unblocked.\n\n    All three endpoints now require authentication (`getCurrentUser` returns `401 Unauthorized` for anonymous requests) and validate the destination URL through `assertSafeUrl` (the same helper that already protects `/api/scrape`) before any outbound `fetch` / `page.goto`, returning `400 Bad Request` for non-HTTP(S) schemes and private/internal IP destinations (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local / cloud-metadata, shared address space, IPv6 ULA / link-local / loopback). The chat citation iframe-fallback feature is unaffected because it runs inside the authenticated chat UI and previews public citation URLs. The `[👣][🧠]` TODO in `isValidAgentUrl` is resolved by keeping that function a pure structural validator and documenting that callers reaching untrusted networks must apply `assertSafeUrl` themselves.\n\n-   Fixed unauthenticated abuse of server-side paid AI APIs in Agents Server. Five route handlers proxied directly to paid third-party providers (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) using the **server's API keys** without any authentication check, so any anonymous client could drain the configured API credit and exhaust quotas by repeatedly calling them. All five routes are now protected by a new shared `guardPaidApiRequest` utility that combines authentication and per-identity sliding-window rate limiting (DRY for all paid-proxy endpoints):\n\n    -   `/api/chat` and `/api/chat-streaming` were OpenAI smoke-test endpoints with no frontend usage. They are now gated behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and return `404` in production so they cannot be exploited even if the deployment exposes them.\n    -   `/api/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions` now requires authentication (signed session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer ptbk_…` API key), enforces a 25 MB upload size limit, validates the `model` parameter against an allowlist of supported OpenAI transcription models (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `whisper-1`), validates `language` against ISO-639-1, and truncates the optional transcription `prompt` to 800 characters.\n    -   `/api/elevenlabs/tts` now requires authentication and validates the caller-supplied `voiceId` against the strict ElevenLabs format (15–40 alphanumeric characters), preventing path-segment injection into the upstream URL and rejecting unknown voices that would still bill the ElevenLabs account.\n    -   `/api/images/[filename]` now requires authentication and validates `modelName`, `size`, `quality`, and `style` query parameters against fixed allowlists (DALL·E / Gemini image models, supported sizes, `standard`/`hd`, `vivid`/`natural`) before forwarding to the paid image generation provider.\n    -   The shared guard applies a per-identity sliding-window rate limit on top of authentication — by username for cookie sessions, by hashed API key for bearer auth, and by request IP for any anonymous fallback. Budgets are tier-specific (60/min for transcription and TTS, 20/min for image generation), so a single compromised account cannot sustain large bills. Rejected requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.\n\n-   Fixed authentication bypass in Agents Server `validateApiKey`: the helper previously treated the presence of any `sessionToken` cookie as proof of a valid browser session, so any client could forge `Cookie: sessionToken=anything` and gain unauthenticated access to every endpoint behind `validateApiKey` (including the OpenAI-compatible chat-completion routes that consume server-side API credits). The helper now parses the cookie value with the existing `parseSessionToken` HMAC-signature verifier and only accepts the request when the signature matches, restoring the original intent of the browser-session shortcut without trusting attacker-supplied cookies.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server directory and chat-sidebar reads for standalone VPS and Supabase deployments:\n\n    -   Added SQLite read indexes for active agent/folder directory scans, chat sidebar lists, and active chat job/timeout polling used by the homepage, agent navigation, and chat pages.\n    -   Added matching PostgreSQL indexes for active agent/folder directory reads and creation-time chat sidebar ordering.\n    -   Invalidated cached active organization snapshots after agent source, visibility, create, delete, and restore mutations so optimized homepage/menu data refreshes immediately.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server admin password verification: all three comparison sites (`isUserGlobalAdmin`, `getCurrentUser`, `authenticateUser`) now use a shared `isAdminPasswordEqual` utility that calls Node.js's `timingSafeEqual` (from the `crypto` module) instead of JavaScript's `===` operator, preventing character-by-character password inference via response-time measurement.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so new agent responses show structured real progress from the queued and preparation phases instead of a synthetic immediate pre-answer:\n\n    -   Queued assistant placeholders now render a progress card with current step, next step, and checklist state.\n    -   The durable chat worker updates that card while it reads context, prepares the agent, checks available tools/inputs, and starts the response.\n    -   The `agent_progress` tool instructions now ask the real agent to report concise user-facing decisions, actions, and results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought or raw technical details.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in the Agents Server `/api/scrape` endpoint:\n\n    -   The endpoint now requires authentication — unauthenticated requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.\n    -   Added URL validation via a new `assertSafeUrl` utility that rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes and destination hostnames that resolve to private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918: `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`, `192.168.x`; loopback `127.x`; link-local / cloud-metadata `169.254.x`; shared address space `100.64.x`; IPv6 ULA, link-local, and loopback). Blocked requests receive a `400 Bad Request` response.\n\n-   Fixed package publishing for `@promptbook/cli` by marking the `ptbk coder server` HTTP/UI helpers as CLI-only instead of never-publishable, matching the existing CLI command import chain.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder find-unwritten` command that lists all prompt sections whose body still contains the `@@@` authoring placeholder:\n\n    -   Prints a summary line (done / for agent / to be written counts) followed by a numbered list of unwritten prompts with their file path, line number, and first summary line.\n    -   Accepts `--priority <n>` to apply the same minimum-priority filter used by `ptbk coder run`.\n    -   Reuses the existing `listPromptsToBeWritten` / `printPromptsToBeWritten` utilities so the detection logic stays in one place.\n\n-   Added `--agent <agent-book-path>` option to `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`:\n\n    -   Accepts a path to a `.book` file (relative to the current working directory) whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt before the task text.\n    -   Can be combined with `--context`: the agent system message is inserted first, followed by the task prompt, and finally the context — so the harness sees agent instructions → task → additional context.\n    -   Example: `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --context AGENTS.md --agent agents/coding-expert.book`\n\n-   `ptbk coder init` now automatically generates 5 prompt boilerplate files after setting up the project configuration.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder server` command that runs the same prompt-processing logic as `ptbk coder run` but keeps the process alive and serves a kanban web UI on a configurable port (default `4441`):\n\n    -   The server polls for new prompt files every 5 seconds instead of exiting when all prompts are done or none are ready, making it suitable as a long-running background service.\n    -   A kanban board at `http://localhost:4441` shows all prompt sections grouped into four columns: **To Do**, **Not Ready**, **Done**, and **Failed**.\n    -   Each card is clickable and opens a Trello-style edit modal where the prompt text can be modified and saved back to the source file immediately.\n    -   A **Play / Pause** button in the browser header is kept in sync with the CLI pause state; clicking it calls the same `requestPause` / `requestResume` functions used by the `p` key in the terminal.\n    -   The HTTP server exposes a small REST API: `GET /api/prompts`, `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/pause`, `POST /api/resume`, and `PUT /api/prompts/update`.\n    -   All options from `ptbk coder run` are supported (`--harness`, `--model`, `--thinking-level`, `--context`, `--test`, `--wait`, `--priority`, `--no-commit`, etc.) plus a new `--port` option (or `PTBK_CODER_SERVER_PORT` env var).\n    -   The frontend source lives in `apps/coder-server/index.html` and is served inline by the Node.js HTTP server (no build step required).\n\n-   Added a VSCode extension (`apps/vscode-extension`) for the Book language that provides syntax highlighting for `.book` and `.ptbk` files. The TextMate grammar (`syntaxes/book.tmLanguage.json`) is dynamically generated from `COMMITMENT_REGISTRY` by running `npm run generate-vscode-grammar`, ensuring the extension always reflects the current set of commitment keywords. Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message.
